celaleyn:100-100.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ تُطِيعُوا فَرِيقًا مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ يَرُدُّوكُمْ بَعْدَ إِيمَانِكُمْ كَافِرِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:101-101.t: ﴿وَكَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ﴾ an interrogative expressing amazement and rebuke ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ تُتْلَى عَلَيْكُمْ آيَاتُ اللَّهِ وَفِيكُمْ رَسُولُهُ وَمَنْ يَعْتَصِمْ﴾ holds fast ﴿بِاللَّهِ فَقَدْ هُدِيَ إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ﴾

celaleyn:102-102.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ﴾ by His being obeyed and not disobeyed, thanked and not shown ingratitude, and remembered and not forgotten. They said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is able to do this?" So it was abrogated by His saying, Exalted is He: {فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ} ("So fear Allah as much as you are able"). ﴿وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ affirming the oneness of Allah.

celaleyn:103-103.t: ﴿وَاعْتَصِمُوا﴾ hold fast ﴿بِحَبْلِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. His religion ﴿جَمِيعًا وَلَا تَفَرَّقُوا﴾ after Islam ﴿وَاذْكُرُوا نِعْمَتَ اللَّهِ﴾ His bestowal of favour ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ O assembly of al-Aws and al-Khazraj ﴿إِذْ كُنْتُمْ﴾ before Islam ﴿أَعْدَاءً فَأَلَّفَ﴾ He brought together ﴿بَيْنَ قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾ through Islam ﴿فَأَصْبَحْتُمْ﴾ so you became ﴿بِنِعْمَتِهِ إِخْوَانًا﴾ in religion and mutual allegiance ﴿وَكُنْتُمْ عَلَى شَفَا﴾ the edge ﴿حُفْرَةٍ مِنَ النَّارِ﴾ with nothing between you and falling into it except that you die as disbelievers ﴿فَأَنْقَذَكُمْ مِنْهَا﴾ through faith ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ just as He has made clear to you what has been mentioned ﴿يُبَيِّنُ اللَّهُ لَكُمْ آيَاتِهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ﴾

celaleyn:104-104.t: ﴿وَلْتَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ أُمَّةٌ يَدْعُونَ إِلَى الْخَيْرِ﴾ Islam ﴿وَيَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَأُولَئِكَ﴾ those who call, command and forbid ﴿هُمُ الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾ the successful. And مِنْ is partitive (li-l-tabʿīḍ), because what has been mentioned is a communal obligation (farḍ kifāya) that is not binding on the whole community and does not befit everyone, such as the ignorant. It has also been said that it is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "so that you be a community".

celaleyn:105-105.t: ﴿وَلَا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ تَفَرَّقُوا﴾ from their religion ﴿وَاخْتَلَفُوا﴾ about it ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ﴾ and they are the Jews and the Christians ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:106-106.t: ﴿يَوْمَ تَبْيَضُّ وُجُوهٌ وَتَسْوَدُّ وُجُوهٌ﴾ i.e. the Day of Resurrection ﴿فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ اسْوَدَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ﴾ and they are the disbelievers; they are cast into the Fire and it is said to them in rebuke: ﴿أَكَفَرْتُمْ بَعْدَ إِيمَانِكُمْ﴾ on the day the covenant was taken ﴿فَذُوقُوا الْعَذَابَ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:107-107.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ ابْيَضَّتْ وُجُوهُهُمْ﴾ and they are the believers ﴿فَفِي رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. His Garden ﴿هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾

celaleyn:108-108.t: ﴿تِلْكَ﴾ i.e. these ayahs ﴿آيَاتُ اللَّهِ نَتْلُوهَا عَلَيْكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿بِالْحَقِّ وَمَا اللَّهُ يُرِيدُ ظُلْمًا لِلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ by seizing them without any crime

celaleyn:109-109.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ as possession, creation and servants ﴿وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ﴾ end up ﴿الْأُمُورُ﴾

celaleyn:110-110.t: ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ O community of Muhammad, in the knowledge of Allah the Exalted ﴿خَيْرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخْرِجَتْ﴾ brought forth ﴿لِلنَّاسِ تَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَتَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَلَوْ آمَنَ أَهْلُ الْكِتَابِ لَكَانَ﴾ faith ﴿خَيْرًا لَهُمْ مِنْهُمُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ such as ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām, may Allah be pleased with him, and his companions ﴿وَأَكْثَرُهُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ﴾ the disbelievers

celaleyn:111-111.t: ﴿لَنْ يَضُرُّوكُمْ﴾ i.e. the Jews, O assembly of Muslims, in anything ﴿إِلَّا أَذًى﴾ with the tongue, by way of insult and threat ﴿وَإِنْ يُقَاتِلُوكُمْ يُوَلُّوكُمُ الْأَدْبَارَ﴾ routed ﴿ثُمَّ لَا يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ against you; rather, victory over them is yours

celaleyn:112-112.t: ﴿ضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذِّلَّةُ أَيْنَ مَا ثُقِفُوا﴾ wherever they are found, so they have no might and no protection ﴿إِلَّا﴾ being ﴿بِحَبْلٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَحَبْلٍ مِنَ النَّاسِ﴾ the believers, which is their covenant with them granting safety on condition of paying the jizya, i.e. they have no protection other than that ﴿وَبَاءُوا﴾ they returned ﴿بِغَضَبٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الْمَسْكَنَةُ ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾ i.e. because they ﴿كَانُوا يَكْفُرُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ الْأَنْبِيَاءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ ذَلِكَ﴾ tawkīd (emphasis) ﴿بِمَا عَصَوْا﴾ the command of Allah ﴿وَكَانُوا يَعْتَدُونَ﴾ going beyond the lawful to the unlawful

celaleyn:113-113.t: ﴿لَيْسُوا﴾ i.e. the People of the Book ﴿سَوَاءً﴾ equal ﴿مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ أُمَّةٌ قَائِمَةٌ﴾ upright, firm upon the truth, such as ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām, may Allah be pleased with him, and his companions ﴿يَتْلُونَ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ آنَاءَ اللَّيْلِ﴾ i.e. in its hours ﴿وَهُمْ يَسْجُدُونَ﴾ they pray; a ḥāl (circumstantial)

celaleyn:114-114.t: ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ بِاللَّهِ وَالْيَوْمِ الْآخِرِ وَيَأْمُرُونَ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَيَنْهَوْنَ عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَيُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ وَأُولَئِكَ﴾ those described with what has been mentioned ﴿مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ and among them are those who are not like that and are not among the righteous

celaleyn:115-115.t: ﴿وَمَا تَفْعَلُوا﴾ with tāʾ, "O community", and with yāʾ [يَفْعَلُوا], i.e. the upright community ﴿مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَلَنْ تُكْفَرُوهُ﴾ in both ways [يُكْفَرُوهُ], i.e. you will not be deprived of its reward; rather, you will be recompensed for it ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِالْمُتَّقِينَ﴾

celaleyn:116-116.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَنْ تُغْنِيَ﴾ ward off ﴿عَنْهُمْ أَمْوَالُهُمْ وَلَا أَوْلَادُهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. from His punishment ﴿شَيْئًا﴾ He singled these two out for mention because a person defends himself sometimes by ransoming with wealth and sometimes by seeking help from his children ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾

celaleyn:117-117.t: ﴿مَثَلُ﴾ the description ﴿مَا يُنْفِقُونَ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers ﴿فِي هَذِهِ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا﴾ in enmity to the Prophet, or as charity and the like ﴿كَمَثَلِ رِيحٍ فِيهَا صِرٌّ﴾ intense heat or cold ﴿أَصَابَتْ حَرْثَ﴾ the crops ﴿قَوْمٍ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ through disbelief and disobedience ﴿فَأَهْلَكَتْهُ﴾ so they derived no benefit from it; likewise their spending is lost and they derive no benefit from it ﴿وَمَا ظَلَمَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ by the loss of their spending ﴿وَلَكِنْ أَنْفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ﴾ through the disbelief that necessitates its loss

celaleyn:118-118.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَتَّخِذُوا بِطَانَةً﴾ intimate friends to whom you disclose your secrets ﴿مِنْ دُونِكُمْ﴾ i.e. other than yourselves, among the Jews, the Christians and the hypocrites ﴿لَا يَأْلُونَكُمْ خَبَالًا﴾ accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e. they will not fall short towards you in corruption ﴿وَدُّوا﴾ they wished ﴿مَا عَنِتُّمْ﴾ i.e. your distress, which is severe harm ﴿قَدْ بَدَتِ﴾ has appeared ﴿الْبَغْضَاءُ﴾ enmity towards you ﴿مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾ through slandering you and informing the idolaters of your secrets ﴿وَمَا تُخْفِي صُدُورُهُمْ﴾ of enmity ﴿أَكْبَرُ قَدْ بَيَّنَّا لَكُمُ الْآيَاتِ﴾ about their enmity ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ that; so do not take them as allies

celaleyn:119-119.t: ﴿هَا﴾ for drawing attention (li-l-tanbīh) ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ O ﴿أُولَاءِ﴾ believers ﴿تُحِبُّونَهُمْ﴾ because of their kinship with you and their friendship ﴿وَلَا يُحِبُّونَكُمْ﴾ because they differ from you in religion ﴿وَتُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْكِتَابِ كُلِّهِ﴾ i.e. in all the scriptures, while they do not believe in your scripture ﴿وَإِذَا لَقُوكُمْ قَالُوا آمَنَّا وَإِذَا خَلَوْا عَضُّوا عَلَيْكُمُ الْأَنَامِلَ﴾ the fingertips ﴿مِنَ الْغَيْظِ﴾ intense anger, at the harmony they see among you. Intense anger is expressed by biting the fingertips figuratively (majāzan), even if there is no biting there ﴿قُلْ مُوتُوا بِغَيْظِكُمْ﴾ i.e. remain in it until death, for you will never see what pleases you ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ﴾ of what is in the hearts, including what these people conceal

celaleyn:120-120.t: ﴿إِنْ تَمْسَسْكُمْ﴾ befalls you ﴿حَسَنَةٌ﴾ a blessing, such as victory and spoils ﴿تَسُؤْهُمْ﴾ it grieves them ﴿وَإِنْ تُصِبْكُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ﴾ such as defeat and drought ﴿يَفْرَحُوا بِهَا﴾ This conditional sentence is connected to the conditional sentence before, and what lies between them is a parenthesis (iʿtirāḍ). The meaning is that they are extreme in their enmity towards you, so why do you take them as allies? So avoid them. ﴿وَإِنْ تَصْبِرُوا﴾ on their harm ﴿وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ Allah in taking them as allies and other things ﴿لَا يَضِرْكُمْ﴾ with kasra on the ḍād and sukūn on the rāʾ, and with ḍamma on it [Translator's note: on the rāʾ] and its doubling [لَا يَضُرُّكُمْ] ﴿كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْئًا إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ with yāʾ and tāʾ ﴿مُحِيطٌ﴾ knowing, so He will recompense them for it

celaleyn:121-121.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember, O Muhammad, ﴿إِذْ غَدَوْتَ مِنْ أَهْلِكَ﴾ from Medina ﴿تُبَوِّئُ﴾ settling ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ مَقَاعِدَ﴾ positions in which they stand ﴿لِلْقِتَالِ وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ﴾ to your words ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of your states. This was the day of Uḥud: the Prophet ﷺ went out with a thousand, or fifty short of that, men, while the idolaters were three thousand. He encamped in the mountain pass on Saturday the seventh of Shawwāl in the year three of the Hijra, placed his back and his army towards Uḥud, straightened their ranks, stationed a troop of archers, appointed ʿAbdullāh ibn Jubayr over them at the foot of the mountain, and said: "Drive them off from us with arrows, so that they do not come at us from behind, and do not leave, whether we are defeated or victorious."

celaleyn:122-122.t: ﴿إِذْ﴾ a badal (substitute) for the إِذْ before it ﴿هَمَّتْ طَائِفَتَانِ مِنْكُمْ﴾ Banū Salima and Banū Ḥāritha, the two wings of the army ﴿أَنْ تَفْشَلَا﴾ that they would lose heart from fighting and turn back, when ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy the hypocrite and his companions turned back and he said: "Why should we get ourselves and our children killed?" and said to Abū Jābir al-Salamī, who had said to him, "I adjure you by Allah regarding your Prophet and yourselves": "If we knew there would be fighting, we would follow you." So Allah made the two of them firm and they did not leave ﴿وَاللَّهُ وَلِيُّهُمَا﴾ their helper ﴿وَعَلَى اللَّهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ let them trust in Him and no one else. And when they were defeated, the following was revealed to remind them of Allah's favour:

celaleyn:123-123.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ نَصَرَكُمُ اللَّهُ بِبَدْرٍ﴾ a place between Mecca and Medina ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ أَذِلَّةٌ﴾ through the smallness of your numbers and weapons ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ His favours

celaleyn:124-124.t: ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) for نَصَرَكُمْ ﴿تَقُولُ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ you promise them, to reassure them ﴿أَلَنْ يَكْفِيَكُمْ أَنْ يُمِدَّكُمْ﴾ aid you ﴿رَبُّكُمْ بِثَلَاثَةِ آلَافٍ مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ مُنْزَلِينَ﴾ with the single (unstressed) and the doubled reading

celaleyn:125-125.t: ﴿بَلَى﴾ that suffices you. In al-Anfāl it is with a thousand, because He first aided them with that, then it became three, then it became five, as He the Exalted said: ﴿إِنْ تَصْبِرُوا﴾ in meeting the enemy ﴿وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ Allah regarding disobedience ﴿وَيَأْتُوكُمْ﴾ i.e. the idolaters ﴿مِنْ فَوْرِهِمْ﴾ their time ﴿هَذَا يُمْدِدْكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ بِخَمْسَةِ آلَافٍ مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ مُسَوِّمِينَ﴾ with kasra and fatḥa on the wāw, i.e. marked. And they were patient, and Allah fulfilled His promise, in that the angels fought alongside them on piebald horses, wearing yellow or white turbans which they let hang down between their shoulders.

celaleyn:126-126.t: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ﴾ i.e. the reinforcement ﴿إِلَّا بُشْرَى لَكُمْ﴾ of victory ﴿وَلِتَطْمَئِنَّ﴾ be at rest ﴿قُلُوبُكُمْ بِهِ﴾ so that it does not panic at the great number of the enemy and your small number ﴿وَمَا النَّصْرُ إِلَّا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ﴾ He grants it to whom He wills; it is not by the great number of troops

celaleyn:127-127.t: ﴿لِيَقْطَعَ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) نَصَرَكُمْ, i.e. to destroy ﴿طَرَفًا مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ through killing and capture ﴿أَوْ يَكْبِتَهُمْ﴾ humiliate them through defeat ﴿فَيَنْقَلِبُوا﴾ return ﴿خَائِبِينَ﴾ not having attained what they sought. And the following was revealed when his front tooth ﷺ was broken and his face was wounded on the day of Uḥud, and he said: "How can a people prosper who have stained the face of their Prophet with blood?"

celaleyn:128-128.t: ﴿لَيْسَ لَكَ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ﴾ rather the matter belongs to Allah, so be patient ﴿أَوْ﴾ in the sense of "until" (ilā an) ﴿يَتُوبَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ through Islam ﴿أَوْ يُعَذِّبَهُمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ ظَالِمُونَ﴾ through disbelief

celaleyn:129-129.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ as possession, creation and servants ﴿يَغْفِرُ لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ forgiveness for [Translator's note: i.e. whom He wills forgiveness for] ﴿وَيُعَذِّبُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ his punishment [Translator's note: i.e. whose punishment He wills] ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ﴾ to His friends ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ towards the people of obedience to Him

celaleyn:130-130.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَأْكُلُوا الرِّبَا أَضْعَافًا مُضَاعَفَةً﴾ with an alif and without it, by your increasing the amount when the term falls due and deferring the demand ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ by abandoning it ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾ succeed

celaleyn:131-131.t: ﴿وَاتَّقُوا النَّارَ الَّتِي أُعِدَّتْ لِلْكَافِرِينَ﴾ lest you be punished with it

celaleyn:132-132.t: ﴿وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:133-133.t: ﴿وَسَارِعُوا﴾ with wāw and without it ﴿إِلَى مَغْفِرَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرْضُهَا السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالْأَرْضُ﴾ i.e. like the breadth of the two if one were joined to the other; and الْعَرْضُ is the width ﴿أُعِدَّتْ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ of Allah, by doing acts of obedience and abandoning acts of disobedience

celaleyn:134-134.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ﴾ in obedience to Allah ﴿فِي السَّرَّاءِ وَالضَّرَّاءِ﴾ ease and hardship ﴿وَالْكَاظِمِينَ الْغَيْظَ﴾ who hold back from acting upon it although able to ﴿وَالْعَافِينَ عَنِ النَّاسِ﴾ those who wronged them, i.e. who forgo punishing them ﴿وَاللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ through these deeds, i.e. He rewards them

celaleyn:135-135.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا فَعَلُوا فَاحِشَةً﴾ a vile sin such as fornication ﴿أَوْ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ through what is less than it, such as kissing ﴿ذَكَرُوا اللَّهَ﴾ i.e. His threat ﴿فَاسْتَغْفَرُوا لِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَمَنْ﴾ i.e. none ﴿يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَلَمْ يُصِرُّوا﴾ persist ﴿عَلَى مَا فَعَلُوا﴾ but rather desisted from it ﴿وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that what they committed is disobedience

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿الم﴾ Allah knows best what He means by it.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿نَزَّلَ عَلَيْكَ﴾ O Muḥammad ﴿الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Quran, joined ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ with truthfulness in its reports ﴿مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ﴾ the scriptures before it ﴿وَأَنْزَلَ التَّوْرَاةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ﴾

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ that is, before its revelation ﴿هُدًى﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) in the sense of "guiding away from error" ﴿لِلنَّاسِ﴾ those who followed them. For the two of them He used «أَنْزَلَ», and for the Quran «نَزَّلَ», which implies repetition, because the two were sent down all at once, unlike it. ﴿وَأَنْزَلَ الْفُرْقَانَ﴾ meaning the scriptures that distinguish between truth and falsehood; it is mentioned after the three so as to include all others besides them ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ the Quran and others ﴿لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ﴾ prevailing in His affair, so nothing prevents Him from fulfilling His promise and His threat ﴿ذُو انْتِقَامٍ﴾ severe punishment of whoever disobeys Him, the like of which no one is able to inflict.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَخْفَى عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ﴾ existing ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ﴾ because of His knowledge of all that occurs in the world, universal and particular. He singled the two out for mention because the senses do not go beyond them.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَوِّرُكُمْ فِي الْأَرْحَامِ كَيْفَ يَشَاءُ﴾ male or female, white or black, and so on ﴿لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ﴾ in His dominion ﴿الْحَكِيمُ﴾ in His making.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ مِنْهُ آيَاتٌ مُحْكَمَاتٌ﴾ clear in their indication ﴿هُنَّ أُمُّ الْكِتَابِ﴾ its foundation, relied upon for rulings ﴿وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَابِهَاتٌ﴾ whose meanings are not understood, such as the openings of the surahs. He made all of it muḥkam in His saying {أُحْكِمَتْ آيَاتُهُ}, in the sense that there is no flaw in it, and mutashābih in His saying {كِتَابًا مُتَشَابِهًا}, in the sense that its parts resemble one another in excellence and truthfulness. ﴿فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ زَيْغٌ﴾ deviation from the truth ﴿فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَابَهَ مِنْهُ ابْتِغَاءَ﴾ seeking ﴿الْفِتْنَةِ﴾ for their ignorant ones, by their falling into doubts and confusion ﴿وَابْتِغَاءَ تَأْوِيلِهِ﴾ its interpretation ﴿وَمَا يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ﴾ its interpretation ﴿إِلَّا اللَّهُ﴾ alone ﴿وَالرَّاسِخُونَ﴾ those firm and well grounded ﴿فِي الْعِلْمِ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿يَقُولُونَ آمَنَّا بِهِ﴾ that is, in the mutashābih, that it is from Allah, though we do not know its meaning ﴿كُلٌّ﴾ of the muḥkam and the mutashābih ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِ رَبِّنَا وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ﴾ with assimilation (idghām) of the tāʾ into the dhāl; that is, takes admonition ﴿إِلَّا أُولُوا الْأَلْبَابِ﴾ people of intellect. And they also say, when they see someone following it:

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغْ قُلُوبَنَا﴾ do not incline them away from the truth by seeking an interpretation of it that does not befit us, as You made the hearts of those people deviate ﴿بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَيْتَنَا﴾ guided us to it ﴿وَهَبْ لَنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ﴾ from You ﴿رَحْمَةً﴾ steadfastness ﴿إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْوَهَّابُ﴾ O [Translator's note: the entry ends with «يَا» ("O"), which belongs with «رَبَّنَا» at the start of the next verse.]

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ جَامِعُ النَّاسِ﴾ You gather them ﴿لِيَوْمٍ﴾ that is, on a day ﴿لَا رَيْبَ﴾ doubt ﴿فِيهِ﴾ it is the Day of Resurrection, and You will recompense them for their deeds as You promised ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ﴾ His appointment for the resurrection. In it there is a shift (iltifāt) away from direct address; and it may be part of the speech of Allah the Exalted. The purpose of the supplication with this is to make clear that their concern is the matter of the Hereafter; and that is why they asked for steadfastness in guidance, so as to attain its reward. The two Shaykhs [al-Bukhārī and Muslim] narrated from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse: {هُوَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ مِنْهُ آيَاتٌ مُحْكَمَاتٌ} to its end, and he said: 'When you see those who follow what is ambiguous in it, those are the ones whom Allah has named, so beware of them.'" And al-Ṭabarānī narrated in al-Kabīr from Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "I fear for my community only three traits," and among them he mentioned "that the Book will be opened for them and the believer will take it seeking its interpretation, and none knows its interpretation except Allah; and those firmly grounded in knowledge say: We believe in it, all is from our Lord; and none takes heed except people of intellect" — the hadith.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَنْ تُغْنِيَ﴾ ward off ﴿عَنْهُمْ أَمْوَالُهُمْ وَلَا أَوْلَادُهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ that is, His punishment ﴿شَيْئًا وَأُولَئِكَ هُمْ وَقُودُ النَّارِ﴾ with fatḥa on the wāw: that with which it is kindled. Their way is [Translator's note: «دَأْبُهُمْ» ("their way is") at the end of this entry introduces ﴿كَدَأْبِ﴾ at the start of the next verse.]

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿كَدَأْبِ﴾ like the custom of ﴿آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ of the nations, such as ʿĀd and Thamūd ﴿كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا فَأَخَذَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ destroyed them ﴿بِذُنُوبِهِمْ﴾ and the clause is explicative of what precedes it ﴿وَاللَّهُ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ﴾ And when the Prophet ﷺ, on his return from Badr, called the Jews to Islam and they said to him, "Do not be deluded by having killed a band of inexperienced Qurashīs who do not know how to fight," there was revealed:

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ O Muḥammad ﴿لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ of the Jews ﴿سَتُغْلَبُونَ﴾ with tāʾ and with yāʾ; in this world, by killing, captivity and the imposition of the jizya — and that did happen ﴿وَتُحْشَرُونَ﴾ in both ways; in the Hereafter ﴿إِلَى جَهَنَّمَ﴾ and you will enter it ﴿وَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ﴾ the bed — it.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿قَدْ كَانَ لَكُمْ آيَةٌ﴾ a lesson; the verb is masculine because of the separation [between it and its subject] ﴿فِي فِئَتَيْنِ﴾ two parties ﴿الْتَقَتَا﴾ on the day of Badr, to fight ﴿فِئَةٌ تُقَاتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ that is, in obedience to Him; they were the Prophet and his Companions, three hundred and thirteen men, with two horses, six coats of mail and eight swords, most of them on foot ﴿وَأُخْرَى كَافِرَةٌ يَرَوْنَهُمْ﴾ that is, the disbelievers ﴿مِثْلَيْهِمْ﴾ that is, [twice] the Muslims, that is, more than them, and they were about a thousand ﴿رَأْيَ الْعَيْنِ﴾ that is, a plain, eyewitness seeing. And Allah gave them victory despite their small number. ﴿وَاللَّهُ يُؤَيِّدُ﴾ strengthens ﴿بِنَصْرِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ to help ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ﴾ which has been mentioned ﴿لَعِبْرَةً لِأُولِي الْأَبْصَارِ﴾ for people of insight. Will you not, then, take a lesson from that and believe?

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿زُيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ حُبُّ الشَّهَوَاتِ﴾ what the soul desires and calls to; Allah made them attractive as a test, or Satan did ﴿مِنَ النِّسَاءِ وَالْبَنِينَ وَالْقَنَاطِيرِ﴾ great amounts of wealth ﴿الْمُقَنْطَرَةِ﴾ heaped up ﴿مِنَ الذَّهَبِ وَالْفِضَّةِ وَالْخَيْلِ الْمُسَوَّمَةِ﴾ fine ﴿وَالْأَنْعَامِ﴾ that is, camels, cattle and sheep ﴿وَالْحَرْثِ﴾ crops ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ what has been mentioned ﴿مَتَاعُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا﴾ enjoyed in it and then it perishes ﴿وَاللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ حُسْنُ الْمَآبِ﴾ the return, and it is Paradise; so one should desire it and nothing else.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ O Muḥammad, to your people ﴿أَؤُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾ shall I inform you ﴿بِخَيْرٍ مِنْ ذَلِكُمْ﴾ the desires mentioned; a question seeking affirmation (istifhām taqrīr) ﴿لِلَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا﴾ idolatry (shirk) ﴿عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ a khabar (predicate) whose mubtadaʾ (subject) is ﴿جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ﴾ that is, destined to abide ﴿فِيهَا﴾ when they enter it ﴿وَأَزْوَاجٌ مُطَهَّرَةٌ﴾ from menstruation and other things considered unclean ﴿وَرِضْوَانٌ﴾ with kasra and ḍamma on its first letter, two dialectal forms; that is, abundant good pleasure ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ﴾ knowing ﴿بِالْعِبَادِ﴾ so He will recompense each of them for his deeds.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) or a badal (substitute) of «الَّذِينَ» before it ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ O ﴿رَبَّنَا إِنَّنَا آمَنَّا﴾ we have believed in You and in Your Messenger ﴿فَاغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ﴾

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿الصَّابِرِينَ﴾ in obedience and in refraining from disobedience; a naʿt (adjective) ﴿وَالصَّادِقِينَ﴾ in faith ﴿وَالْقَانِتِينَ﴾ obedient to Allah ﴿وَالْمُنْفِقِينَ﴾ giving charity ﴿وَالْمُسْتَغْفِرِينَ﴾ Allah, by saying "O Allah, forgive us" ﴿بِالْأَسْحَارِ﴾ the last parts of the night; they are singled out for mention because they are a time of heedlessness and the pleasure of sleep.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿شَهِدَ اللَّهُ﴾ He made clear to His creation through proofs and signs ﴿أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ﴾ that is, there is none truly worshipped in existence ﴿إِلَّا هُوَ وَ﴾ testified to that ﴿الْمَلَائِكَةُ﴾ by affirmation ﴿وَأُولُوا الْعِلْمِ﴾ of the prophets and believers, by belief and by word ﴿قَائِمًا﴾ in managing what He has made; it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and what governs it (al-ʿāmil) is the meaning of the clause, that is, "He alone is" ﴿بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ with justice ﴿لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ﴾ He repeated it for tawkīd (emphasis) ﴿الْعَزِيزُ﴾ in His dominion ﴿الْحَكِيمُ﴾ in His making.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿إِنَّ الدِّينَ﴾ that is pleasing ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ is ﴿الْإِسْلَامُ﴾ that is, the law with which the messengers were sent, built upon tawḥīd. In one reading with fatḥa [أَنَّ], as a badal (substitute) of «أَنَّهُ…», a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl). ﴿وَمَا اخْتَلَفَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Jews and Christians, in religion, in that some affirmed Allah's oneness and some disbelieved ﴿إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَهُمُ الْعِلْمُ﴾ of tawḥīd ﴿بَغْيًا﴾ on the part of the disbelievers ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ﴾ that is, of recompensing him.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿فَإِنْ حَاجُّوكَ﴾ the disbelievers dispute with you, O Muḥammad, about religion ﴿فَقُلْ﴾ to them ﴿أَسْلَمْتُ وَجْهِيَ﴾ I have submitted to Him — I ﴿وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَنِ﴾ The face is singled out for mention because of its nobility, so the rest is all the more so. ﴿وَقُلْ لِلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Jews and Christians ﴿وَالْأُمِّيِّينَ﴾ the idolaters of the Arabs ﴿أَأَسْلَمْتُمْ﴾ that is, submit! ﴿فَإِنْ أَسْلَمُوا فَقَدِ اهْتَدَوْا﴾ out of error ﴿وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا﴾ from Islam ﴿فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ الْبَلَاغُ﴾ conveying the message ﴿وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِالْعِبَادِ﴾ so He will recompense them for their deeds. This was before the command to fight.

celaleyn:136-136.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ جَزَاؤُهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ وَجَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا﴾ a ḥāl muqaddara (anticipated circumstantial), i.e. with abiding in it decreed for them once they enter it ﴿وَنِعْمَ أَجْرُ الْعَامِلِينَ﴾ in obedience is this reward. And the following was revealed concerning the defeat at Uḥud:

celaleyn:137-137.t: ﴿قَدْ خَلَتْ﴾ have passed ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ سُنَنٌ﴾ ways with the disbelievers, of granting them respite and then seizing them ﴿فَسِيرُوا﴾ O believers ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ فَانْظُرُوا كَيْفَ كَانَ عَاقِبَةُ الْمُكَذِّبِينَ﴾ of the messengers, i.e. the final outcome of their affair, in destruction; so do not grieve at their gaining the upper hand, for I am granting them respite until their appointed time

celaleyn:138-138.t: ﴿هَذَا﴾ the Quran ﴿بَيَانٌ لِلنَّاسِ﴾ all of them ﴿وَهُدًى﴾ from misguidance ﴿وَمَوْعِظَةٌ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ among them

celaleyn:139-139.t: ﴿وَلَا تَهِنُوا﴾ weaken from fighting the disbelievers ﴿وَلَا تَحْزَنُوا﴾ over what befell you at Uḥud ﴿وَأَنْتُمُ الْأَعْلَوْنَ﴾ by prevailing over them ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ truly; and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is indicated by the whole of what precedes it

celaleyn:140-140.t: ﴿إِنْ يَمْسَسْكُمْ﴾ befalls you at Uḥud ﴿قَرْحٌ﴾ with fatḥa and ḍamma on the qāf: hardship from a wound and the like ﴿فَقَدْ مَسَّ الْقَوْمَ﴾ the disbelievers ﴿قَرْحٌ مِثْلُهُ﴾ at Badr ﴿وَتِلْكَ الْأَيَّامُ نُدَاوِلُهَا﴾ We turn them about ﴿بَيْنَ النَّاسِ﴾ one day for one party and one day for another, so that they take heed ﴿وَلِيَعْلَمَ اللَّهُ﴾ with a knowledge of manifestation ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ who are sincere in their faith, from others ﴿وَيَتَّخِذَ مِنْكُمْ شُهَدَاءَ﴾ honouring them with martyrdom ﴿وَاللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the disbelievers, i.e. He punishes them, and the blessings He bestows on them are a gradual leading to ruin (istidrāj)

celaleyn:141-141.t: ﴿وَلِيُمَحِّصَ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ purify them of sins through what befalls them ﴿وَيَمْحَقَ﴾ destroy ﴿الْكَافِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:142-142.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ i.e. "rather, did" (bal a-) ﴿حَسِبْتُمْ أَنْ تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ وَلَمَّا﴾ not (lam) ﴿يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ جَاهَدُوا مِنْكُمْ﴾ with a knowledge of manifestation ﴿وَيَعْلَمَ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾ in hardships

celaleyn:143-143.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ كُنْتُمْ تَمَنَّوْنَ﴾ in it one of the two tāʾs of the original form is omitted ﴿الْمَوْتَ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَلْقَوْهُ﴾ when you said: "Would that we had a day like the day of Badr, so that we might attain what its martyrs attained" ﴿فَقَدْ رَأَيْتُمُوهُ﴾ i.e. its cause, war ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ تَنْظُرُونَ﴾ i.e. seeing, considering how the situation is; so why were you routed? And the following was revealed concerning their defeat, when it was rumoured that the Prophet had been killed and the hypocrites said to them: "If he has been killed, then return to your religion":

celaleyn:144-144.t: ﴿وَمَا مُحَمَّدٌ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ الرُّسُلُ أَفَإِنْ مَاتَ أَوْ قُتِلَ﴾ like others ﴿انْقَلَبْتُمْ عَلَى أَعْقَابِكُمْ﴾ you returned to disbelief. The last clause is the locus of the interrogative of denial (al-istifhām al-inkārī), i.e. he was not one to be worshipped, such that you would turn back ﴿وَمَنْ يَنْقَلِبْ عَلَى عَقِبَيْهِ فَلَنْ يَضُرَّ اللَّهَ شَيْئًا﴾ rather he harms only himself ﴿وَسَيَجْزِي اللَّهُ الشَّاكِرِينَ﴾ of His favours, by standing firm

celaleyn:145-145.t: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفْسٍ أَنْ تَمُوتَ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ by His decree ﴿كِتَابًا﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. Allah has written that ﴿مُؤَجَّلًا﴾ fixed in time, neither advanced nor delayed. So why were you routed! Defeat does not ward off death, and standing firm does not cut life short ﴿وَمَنْ يُرِدْ﴾ by his deed ﴿ثَوَابَ الدُّنْيَا﴾ i.e. its recompense from it ﴿نُؤْتِهِ مِنْهَا﴾ what has been allotted to him, and he has no share in the Hereafter ﴿وَمَنْ يُرِدْ ثَوَابَ الْآخِرَةِ نُؤْتِهِ مِنْهَا﴾ i.e. of its reward ﴿وَسَنَجْزِي الشَّاكِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:146-146.t: ﴿وَكَأَيِّنْ﴾ how many ﴿مِنْ نَبِيٍّ قُتِلَ﴾ and in one reading [قَاتَلَ] ("fought"), the fāʿil (agent) being its pronoun ﴿مَعَهُ﴾ a khabar (predicate) whose mubtadaʾ (subject) is ﴿رِبِّيُّونَ كَثِيرٌ﴾ many multitudes ﴿فَمَا وَهَنُوا﴾ they did not lose heart ﴿لِمَا أَصَابَهُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ of wounds and the killing of their prophets and companions ﴿وَمَا ضَعُفُوا﴾ from jihad ﴿وَمَا اسْتَكَانُوا﴾ submit to their enemy, as you did when it was said the Prophet had been killed ﴿وَاللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾ in trial, i.e. He rewards them

celaleyn:147-147.t: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ قَوْلَهُمْ﴾ when their prophet was killed, together with their firmness and patience ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ قَالُوا رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَإِسْرَافَنَا﴾ our overstepping the limit ﴿فِي أَمْرِنَا﴾ an indication that what befell them was due to their bad deeds, and in self-abasement ﴿وَثَبِّتْ أَقْدَامَنَا﴾ with strength for jihad ﴿وَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:148-148.t: ﴿فَآتَاهُمُ اللَّهُ ثَوَابَ الدُّنْيَا﴾ victory and spoils ﴿وَحُسْنَ ثَوَابِ الْآخِرَةِ﴾ i.e. the Garden; its goodness is bounty beyond what is deserved ﴿وَاللَّهُ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:149-149.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ تُطِيعُوا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ in what they command you ﴿يَرُدُّوكُمْ عَلَى أَعْقَابِكُمْ﴾ to disbelief ﴿فَتَنْقَلِبُوا خَاسِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:150-150.t: ﴿بَلِ اللَّهُ مَوْلَاكُمْ﴾ your helper ﴿وَهُوَ خَيْرُ النَّاصِرِينَ﴾ so obey Him rather than them

celaleyn:151-151.t: ﴿سَنُلْقِي فِي قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الرُّعْبَ﴾ with sukūn and ḍamma on the ʿayn: fear. After departing from Uḥud they had resolved to return and annihilate the Muslims, but they were struck with terror and did not return ﴿بِمَا أَشْرَكُوا﴾ because of their associating ﴿بِاللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يُنَزِّلْ بِهِ سُلْطَانًا﴾ a proof for its worship, namely the idols ﴿وَمَأْوَاهُمُ النَّارُ وَبِئْسَ مَثْوَى﴾ the abode ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the disbelievers, is it

celaleyn:152-152.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ صَدَقَكُمُ اللَّهُ وَعْدَهُ﴾ to you of victory ﴿إِذْ تَحُسُّونَهُمْ﴾ you were killing them ﴿بِإِذْنِهِ﴾ by His will ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا فَشِلْتُمْ﴾ you lost heart from fighting ﴿وَتَنَازَعْتُمْ﴾ you disagreed ﴿فِي الْأَمْرِ﴾ i.e. the command of the Prophet ﷺ to stay at the foot of the mountain for shooting: some of you said, "Let us go, for our companions have been victorious," and some of you, "We will not disobey the command of the Prophet ﷺ" ﴿وَعَصَيْتُمْ﴾ his command, and left the position in pursuit of spoils ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا أَرَاكُمْ﴾ Allah ﴿مَا تُحِبُّونَ﴾ of victory. The apodosis of إِذَا is indicated by what precedes it, i.e. He withheld His help from you ﴿مِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرِيدُ الدُّنْيَا﴾ and so left the position for spoils ﴿وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرِيدُ الْآخِرَةَ﴾ and so stood firm in it until he was killed, such as ʿAbdullāh ibn Jubayr and his companions ﴿ثُمَّ صَرَفَكُمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the implied apodosis of إِذَا; He turned you back in defeat ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ i.e. the disbelievers ﴿لِيَبْتَلِيَكُمْ﴾ to test you, so that the sincere would be distinguished from the others ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَفَا عَنْكُمْ﴾ what you committed ﴿وَاللَّهُ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ through pardon. Remember

celaleyn:153-153.t: ﴿إِذْ تُصْعِدُونَ﴾ going far off in the land, fleeing ﴿وَلَا تَلْوُونَ﴾ turning aside ﴿عَلَى أَحَدٍ وَالرَّسُولُ يَدْعُوكُمْ فِي أُخْرَاكُمْ﴾ i.e. from behind you, saying: "To me, servants of Allah! To me, servants of Allah!" ﴿فَأَثَابَكُمْ﴾ so He recompensed you ﴿غَمًّا﴾ through the defeat ﴿بِغَمٍّ﴾ because of your distressing the Messenger by disobedience. It has also been said that the bāʾ is in the sense of عَلَى ("upon"), i.e. doubled upon the distress of missing the spoils ﴿لِكَيْلَا﴾ attached to عَفَا or to أَثَابَكُمْ, and {لَا} is redundant (zāʾida) ﴿تَحْزَنُوا عَلَى مَا فَاتَكُمْ﴾ of the spoils ﴿وَلَا مَا أَصَابَكُمْ﴾ of killing and defeat ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَبِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:154-154.t: ﴿ثُمَّ أَنْزَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِ الْغَمِّ أَمَنَةً﴾ security ﴿نُعَاسًا﴾ a badal (substitute) ﴿يَغْشَى﴾ with yāʾ and tāʾ ﴿طَائِفَةً مِنْكُمْ﴾ and they are the believers; they were swaying under their leather shields and their swords were falling from them ﴿وَطَائِفَةٌ قَدْ أَهَمَّتْهُمْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ﴾ i.e. drove them to anxiety, so they had no desire except their own safety, not that of the Prophet and his companions, and they did not sleep; they are the hypocrites ﴿يَظُنُّونَ بِاللَّهِ﴾ a thought ﴿غَيْرَ﴾ the thought ﴿الْحَقِّ ظَنَّ﴾ i.e. like the thought ﴿الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ﴾ in that they believed that the Prophet had been killed or would not be helped ﴿يَقُولُونَ هَلْ﴾ i.e. not (mā) ﴿لَنَا مِنَ الْأَمْرِ﴾ i.e. the victory we were promised ﴿مِنْ﴾ redundant ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿إِنَّ الْأَمْرَ كُلَّهُ﴾ in the accusative as tawkīd (emphasis), and in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ i.e. the decree belongs to Him; He does what He wills ﴿يُخْفُونَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِمْ مَا لَا يُبْدُونَ﴾ show ﴿لَكَ يَقُولُونَ﴾ an explanation (bayān) of what precedes it ﴿لَوْ كَانَ لَنَا مِنَ الْأَمْرِ شَيْءٌ مَا قُتِلْنَا هَاهُنَا﴾ i.e. had the choice been ours we would not have gone out and so would not have been killed, but he made us go out against our will ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿لَوْ كُنْتُمْ فِي بُيُوتِكُمْ﴾ and among you were those on whom Allah had written death by killing ﴿لَبَرَزَ﴾ would have gone out ﴿الَّذِينَ كُتِبَ﴾ decreed ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ الْقَتْلُ﴾ among you ﴿إِلَى مَضَاجِعِهِمْ﴾ the places where they fall, and they would have been killed, and their staying behind would not have saved them, because His decree, Exalted is He, comes to pass without fail ﴿وَ﴾ He did what He did at Uḥud ﴿لِيَبْتَلِيَ﴾ to test ﴿اللَّهُ مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ﴾ your hearts, of sincerity and hypocrisy ﴿وَلِيُمَحِّصَ﴾ to distinguish ﴿مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ﴾ of what is in the hearts; nothing is hidden from Him, and He tests only so that it becomes manifest to people

celaleyn:155-155.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوْا مِنْكُمْ﴾ from fighting ﴿يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعَانِ﴾ the host of the Muslims and the host of the disbelievers at Uḥud; and they are the Muslims except for twelve men ﴿إِنَّمَا اسْتَزَلَّهُمْ﴾ caused them to slip ﴿الشَّيْطَانُ﴾ by his whispering ﴿بِبَعْضِ مَا كَسَبُوا﴾ of sins, namely disobeying the command of the Prophet ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَفَا اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ﴾ to the believers ﴿حَلِيمٌ﴾ He does not hasten against the disobedient

celaleyn:156-156.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ i.e. the hypocrites ﴿وَقَالُوا لِإِخْوَانِهِمْ﴾ i.e. concerning them ﴿إِذَا ضَرَبُوا﴾ travelled ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ and died ﴿أَوْ كَانُوا غُزًّى﴾ plural of غَازٍ ("raider"), and were killed ﴿لَوْ كَانُوا عِنْدَنَا مَا مَاتُوا وَمَا قُتِلُوا﴾ i.e. do not speak as they speak ﴿لِيَجْعَلَ اللَّهُ ذَلِكَ﴾ saying, in the end result of their affair ﴿حَسْرَةً فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ وَاللَّهُ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ﴾ so staying behind does not hold back death ﴿وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ with tāʾ and yāʾ ﴿بَصِيرٌ﴾ so He will recompense you for it

celaleyn:157-157.t: ﴿وَلَئِنْ﴾ the lām of oath ﴿قُتِلْتُمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. jihad ﴿أَوْ مُتُّمْ﴾ with ḍamma and kasra on the mīm, from مَاتَ يَمُوتُ and يَمَاتُ; death came to you in it ﴿لَمَغْفِرَةٌ﴾ existing ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ for your sins ﴿وَرَحْمَةٌ﴾ from Him for you for that. The lām and what it enters upon are the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), and it is in the place of the verb; a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿خَيْرٌ مِمَّا تَجْمَعُونَ﴾ of this world, with tāʾ and yāʾ [يَجْمَعُونَ]

celaleyn:158-158.t: ﴿وَلَئِنْ﴾ the lām of oath ﴿مُتُّمْ﴾ in both ways ﴿أَوْ قُتِلْتُمْ﴾ in jihad or otherwise ﴿لَإِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ and not to anyone else ﴿تُحْشَرُونَ﴾ in the Hereafter, and He will recompense you

celaleyn:159-159.t: ﴿فَبِمَا﴾ مَا is redundant (zāʾida) ﴿رَحْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ لِنْتَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ i.e. you made your manner easy when they opposed you ﴿وَلَوْ كُنْتَ فَظًّا﴾ ill-mannered ﴿غَلِيظَ الْقَلْبِ﴾ harsh, and had been rough with them ﴿لَانْفَضُّوا﴾ they would have dispersed ﴿مِنْ حَوْلِكَ فَاعْفُ﴾ pass over ﴿عَنْهُمْ﴾ what they did ﴿وَاسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ﴾ their sin, so that I forgive them ﴿وَشَاوِرْهُمْ﴾ draw out their opinions ﴿فِي الْأَمْرِ﴾ i.e. your affairs of war and other things, to put their hearts at ease and so that you would be followed as an example. And he ﷺ consulted them often ﴿فَإِذَا عَزَمْتَ﴾ upon carrying out what you want after consultation ﴿فَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ trust in Him, not in the consultation ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَوَكِّلِينَ﴾ on Him

celaleyn:160-160.t: ﴿إِنْ يَنْصُرْكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ helps you against your enemy, as on the day of Badr ﴿فَلَا غَالِبَ لَكُمْ وَإِنْ يَخْذُلْكُمْ﴾ by withholding His help from you, as on the day of Uḥud ﴿فَمَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَنْصُرُكُمْ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ﴾ i.e. after His forsaking, i.e. you have no helper ﴿وَعَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ and no other ﴿فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ﴾ let them trust ﴿الْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ And the following was revealed when a red velvet cloak went missing on the day of Badr and some people said: "Perhaps the Prophet took it."

celaleyn:161-161.t: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ﴾ it is not fitting ﴿لِنَبِيٍّ أَنْ يَغُلَّ﴾ to act dishonestly with the spoils, so do not think that of him; and in one reading it is passive (bi-l-bināʾ li-l-mafʿūl), i.e. to be attributed to dishonesty with the spoils ﴿وَمَنْ يَغْلُلْ يَأْتِ بِمَا غَلَّ يَوْمَ الْقِيمَةِ﴾ carrying it on his neck ﴿ثُمَّ تُوَفَّى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ﴾ the dishonest one and others, the recompense of ﴿مَا كَسَبَتْ﴾ it did ﴿وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ in anything

celaleyn:162-162.t: ﴿أَفَمَنِ اتَّبَعَ رِضْوَانَ اللَّهِ﴾ and so obeyed and did not act dishonestly ﴿كَمَنْ بَاءَ﴾ returned ﴿بِسَخَطٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ because of his disobedience and dishonesty ﴿وَمَأْوَاهُ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ i.e. the place of return is it

celaleyn:163-163.t: ﴿هُمْ دَرَجَاتٌ﴾ i.e. possessors of degrees ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. of differing ranks: for the one who followed His good pleasure is the reward, and for the one who returned with His displeasure is the punishment ﴿وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ so He will recompense them for it

celaleyn:164-164.t: ﴿لَقَدْ مَنَّ اللَّهُ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِذْ بَعَثَ فِيهِمْ رَسُولًا مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ i.e. an Arab like them, so that they would understand him and be honoured by him, not an angel nor a non-Arab ﴿يَتْلُو عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتِهِ﴾ the Quran ﴿وَيُزَكِّيهِمْ﴾ purifies them from sins ﴿وَيُعَلِّمُهُمُ الْكِتَابَ﴾ the Quran ﴿وَالْحِكْمَةَ﴾ the Sunna ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ lightened (mukhaffafa), i.e. "indeed they" ﴿كَانُوا مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ i.e. before his being sent ﴿لَفِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ clear

celaleyn:165-165.t: ﴿أَوَ لَمَّا أَصَابَتْكُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ﴾ at Uḥud, with the killing of seventy of you ﴿قَدْ أَصَبْتُمْ مِثْلَيْهَا﴾ at Badr, with the killing of seventy and the capture of seventy of them ﴿قُلْتُمْ﴾ in amazement ﴿أَنَّى﴾ from where do we get ﴿هَذَا﴾ forsaking, when we are Muslims and the Messenger of Allah is among us? The last clause is the locus of the interrogative of denial (al-istifhām al-inkārī) ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿هُوَ مِنْ عِنْدِ أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ because you left the position and so were forsaken ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ including victory and withholding it, and He has recompensed you for your disobedience

celaleyn:166-166.t: ﴿وَمَا أَصَابَكُمْ يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعَانِ﴾ at Uḥud ﴿فَبِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ by His will ﴿وَلِيَعْلَمَ﴾ Allah, with a knowledge of manifestation ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ truly

celaleyn:167-167.t: ﴿وَلِيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ نَافَقُوا وَ﴾ those who ﴿قِيلَ لَهُمْ﴾ when they turned away from the fighting, and they are ʿAbdullāh ibn Ubayy and his companions ﴿تَعَالَوْا قَاتِلُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ His enemies ﴿أَوِ ادْفَعُوا﴾ the people from us, by increasing your numbers, if you will not fight ﴿قَالُوا لَوْ نَعْلَمُ﴾ were good at ﴿قِتَالًا لَاتَّبَعْنَاكُمْ﴾ He the Exalted said, giving them the lie: ﴿هُمْ لِلْكُفْرِ يَوْمَئِذٍ أَقْرَبُ مِنْهُمْ لِلْإِيمَانِ﴾ because of the forsaking of the believers they displayed, whereas before they were closer to faith as far as outward appearance goes ﴿يَقُولُونَ بِأَفْوَاهِهِمْ مَا لَيْسَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ for even if they knew of fighting they would not follow you ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يَكْتُمُونَ﴾ of hypocrisy

celaleyn:168-168.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a badal (substitute) for the الَّذِينَ before it, or a naʿt (adjective) ﴿قَالُوا لِإِخْوَانِهِمْ﴾ in religion ﴿وَ﴾ having (qad) ﴿قَعَدُوا﴾ from jihad ﴿لَوْ أَطَاعُونَا﴾ i.e. the martyrs of Uḥud, or our brothers in staying behind ﴿مَا قُتِلُوا قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿فَادْرَءُوا﴾ ward off ﴿عَنْ أَنْفُسِكُمُ الْمَوْتَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ in that staying behind saves from it. And the following was revealed concerning the martyrs:

celaleyn:169-169.t: ﴿وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ قُتِلُوا﴾ with the single (unstressed) and the doubled reading ﴿فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. for the sake of His religion ﴿أَمْوَاتًا بَلْ﴾ they are ﴿أَحْيَاءٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ their souls are in the crops of green birds that roam freely in the Garden wherever they wish, as has come in the hadith ﴿يُرْزَقُونَ﴾ they eat of the fruits of the Garden

celaleyn:170-170.t: ﴿فَرِحِينَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of يُرْزَقُونَ ﴿بِمَا آتَاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ وَ﴾ they ﴿يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ﴾ rejoice ﴿بِالَّذِينَ لَمْ يَلْحَقُوا بِهِمْ مِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ﴾ of their believing brothers; and from الَّذِينَ is substituted (badal) ﴿أَنْ﴾ i.e. "that" (bi-an) ﴿لَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ i.e. those who have not joined them ﴿وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ in the Hereafter. The meaning is: they rejoice at their safety and their joy.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَكْفُرُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ وَيَقْتُلُونَ﴾ and in one reading [يُقَاتِلُونَ] ﴿النَّبِيِّينَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ وَيَقْتُلُونَ الَّذِينَ يَأْمُرُونَ بِالْقِسْطِ﴾ with justice ﴿مِنَ النَّاسِ﴾ and they are the Jews. It is narrated that they killed forty-three prophets; then a hundred and seventy of their devout men forbade them, and they killed them that same day. ﴿فَبَشِّرْهُمْ﴾ inform them ﴿بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾ painful. The mention of "good tidings" is in mockery of them. The fāʾ enters the khabar (predicate) of «إِنَّ» because its noun, a relative noun, resembles a condition.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ حَبِطَتْ﴾ have become void ﴿أَعْمَالُهُمْ﴾ the good they did, such as charity and maintaining ties of kinship ﴿فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ so they count for nothing, because their condition is lacking ﴿وَمَا لَهُمْ مِنْ نَاصِرِينَ﴾ protecting them from the punishment.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ﴾ look ﴿إِلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا نَصِيبًا﴾ a share ﴿مِنَ الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Torah ﴿يُدْعَوْنَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿إِلَى كِتَابِ اللَّهِ لِيَحْكُمَ بَيْنَهُمْ ثُمَّ يَتَوَلَّى فَرِيقٌ مِنْهُمْ وَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ from accepting its judgement. It was revealed about the Jews: two of them committed adultery, and they took the case to the Prophet ﷺ, who ruled that the two be stoned. They refused; the Torah was brought and it was found in it, so the two were stoned, and they were angered.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ turning away and aversion ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوا﴾ that is, because of their saying ﴿لَنْ تَمَسَّنَا النَّارُ إِلَّا أَيَّامًا مَعْدُودَاتٍ﴾ forty days, the period of their forefathers' worship of the calf, after which it will leave them ﴿وَغَرَّهُمْ فِي دِينِهِمْ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) His saying ﴿مَا كَانُوا يَفْتَرُونَ﴾ in that saying of theirs.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿فَكَيْفَ﴾ will be their state ﴿إِذَا جَمَعْنَاهُمْ لِيَوْمٍ﴾ that is, on a day ﴿لَا رَيْبَ﴾ doubt ﴿فِيهِ﴾ it is the Day of Resurrection ﴿وَوُفِّيَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ﴾ of the People of the Book and others, the recompense of ﴿مَا كَسَبَتْ﴾ what it did of good and evil ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ that is, people ﴿لَا يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ by the reduction of a good deed or the addition of an evil deed. And when he ﷺ promised his community the dominion of Persia and Byzantium, and the hypocrites said, "Far from it!", there was revealed:

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ﴾ O Allah ﴿مَالِكَ الْمُلْكِ تُؤْتِي﴾ You give ﴿الْمُلْكَ مَنْ تَشَاءُ﴾ of Your creation ﴿وَتَنْزِعُ الْمُلْكَ مِمَّنْ تَشَاءُ وَتُعِزُّ مَنْ تَشَاءُ﴾ by giving it to him ﴿وَتُذِلُّ مَنْ تَشَاءُ﴾ by taking it from him ﴿بِيَدِكَ﴾ by Your power ﴿الْخَيْرُ﴾ that is, and the evil ﴿إِنَّكَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿تُولِجُ﴾ You make enter ﴿اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهَارِ وَتُولِجُ النَّهَارَ﴾ You make it enter ﴿فِي اللَّيْلِ﴾ so each of them increases by what the other loses ﴿وَتُخْرِجُ الْحَيَّ مِنَ الْمَيِّتِ﴾ such as man and the bird from the sperm-drop and the egg ﴿وَتُخْرِجُ الْمَيِّتَ﴾ such as the sperm-drop and the egg ﴿مِنَ الْحَيِّ وَتَرْزُقُ مَنْ تَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ﴾ that is, ample provision.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿لَا يَتَّخِذِ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ الْكَافِرِينَ أَوْلِيَاءَ﴾ taking them as allies ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ that is, other than ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ﴾ that is, takes them as allies ﴿فَلَيْسَ مِنَ﴾ the religion of ﴿اللَّهِ فِي شَيْءٍ إِلَّا أَنْ تَتَّقُوا مِنْهُمْ تُقَاةً﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun) of تَقَيْتُهُ; that is, you fear [them] with a fear, in which case you may show them alliance with the tongue but not the heart. This was before Islam became strong, and it applies to whoever is in a land where he is not strong. ﴿وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ﴾ warns you ﴿اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ﴾ that He will be angry with you if you ally with them ﴿وَإِلَى اللَّهِ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ the return, and He will recompense you.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿إِنْ تُخْفُوا مَا فِي صُدُورِكُمْ﴾ your hearts, of alliance with them ﴿أَوْ تُبْدُوهُ﴾ show it ﴿يَعْلَمْهُ اللَّهُ وَ﴾ He ﴿يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ including punishing whoever allies with them.

celaleyn:30-30.t: Mention ﴿يَوْمَ تَجِدُ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَا عَمِلَتْ﴾ [the implied] it ﴿مِنْ خَيْرٍ مُحْضَرًا وَمَا عَمِلَتْ﴾ [the implied] it ﴿مِنْ سُوءٍ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿تَوَدُّ لَوْ أَنَّ بَيْنَهَا وَبَيْنَهُ أَمَدًا بَعِيدًا﴾ an extremely distant limit, so that it would not reach her ﴿وَيُحَذِّرُكُمُ اللَّهُ نَفْسَهُ﴾ repeated for tawkīd (emphasis) ﴿وَاللَّهُ رَءُوفٌ بِالْعِبَادِ﴾ And when they said, "We worship the idols only out of love for Allah, so that they may bring us near to Him," there was revealed:

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them, O Muḥammad ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تُحِبُّونَ اللَّهَ فَاتَّبِعُونِي يُحْبِبْكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ in the sense that He will reward you ﴿وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ ذُنُوبَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ﴾ to whoever follows me, for what he did before that ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ to him.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ﴾ in what he commands you of tawḥīd ﴿فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا﴾ turned away from obedience ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ In it the overt noun is put in place of the pronoun; that is, He does not love them, in the sense that He will punish them.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَى﴾ chose ﴿آدَمَ وَنُوحًا وَآلَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَآلَ عِمْرَانَ﴾ meaning the two of them themselves ﴿عَلَى الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ by making the prophets from their descendants.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿ذُرِّيَّةً بَعْضُهَا مِنْ﴾ the offspring of ﴿بَعْضٍ﴾ of them ﴿وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ Mention

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿إِذْ قَالَتِ امْرَأَتُ عِمْرَانَ﴾ Ḥanna, when she had grown old and longed for a child, so she prayed to Allah and felt herself pregnant: O ﴿رَبِّ إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ﴾ to make ﴿لَكَ مَا فِي بَطْنِي مُحَرَّرًا﴾ freed, devoted, clear of worldly concerns, for the service of Your Holy House ﴿فَتَقَبَّلْ مِنِّي إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of supplication ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of intentions. And ʿImrān died while she was pregnant.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا وَضَعَتْهَا﴾ gave birth to her, a girl — she had hoped it would be a boy, since only boys were dedicated — ﴿قَالَتْ﴾ apologetically: O ﴿رَبِّ إِنِّي وَضَعْتُهَا أُنْثَى وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ﴾ that is, knowing ﴿بِمَا وَضَعَتْ﴾ a parenthetical clause (jumla iʿtirāḍiyya) from the speech of the Exalted; and in one reading with ḍamma on the tāʾ ﴿وَلَيْسَ الذَّكَرُ﴾ that she sought ﴿كَالْأُنْثَى﴾ that was given, because he would be intended for service, and she is not suited to it because of her weakness, her being ʿawra, and the menstruation and the like that befall her ﴿وَإِنِّي سَمَّيْتُهَا مَرْيَمَ وَإِنِّي أُعِيذُهَا بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَهَا﴾ her children ﴿مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ﴾ the outcast. In the hadith: "There is no child born but Satan touches him when he is born, and he cries out, except Maryam and her son." Narrated by the two Shaykhs [al-Bukhārī and Muslim].

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿فَتَقَبَّلَهَا رَبُّهَا﴾ that is, He accepted Maryam from her mother ﴿بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍ وَأَنْبَتَهَا نَبَاتًا حَسَنًا﴾ He brought her up with a fine character; she would grow in a day as a newborn grows in a year. Her mother brought her to the rabbis, the custodians of Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis), and said: "Here is this dedicated one." They competed for her because she was the daughter of their imam. Zakariyyā said: "I have the best right to her, because her maternal aunt is my wife." They said: "No, not until we cast lots." So they went, twenty-nine of them, to the river Jordan and threw in their pens, on the understanding that whoever's pen stood firm in the water and rose up would have the better right to her. Zakariyyā's pen stood firm, so he took her and built her a chamber in the mosque with a ladder by which no one but he went up to her. He used to bring her food, drink and oil, and would find with her the fruit of summer in winter and the fruit of winter in summer, as the Exalted said: ﴿وَكَفَلَهَا زَكَرِيَّاءُ﴾ he took her into his care. In one reading [وَكَفَّلَهَا زَكَرِيَّا], with tashdīd and with زَكَرِيَّا in the accusative, with and without the long final alif (mamdūd and maqṣūr); the fāʿil (agent) is Allah. ﴿كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا زَكَرِيَّاءُ [زَكَرِيَّا] الْمِحْرَابَ﴾ the chamber, which is the noblest of places to sit ﴿وَجَدَ عِنْدَهَا رِزْقًا قَالَ يَا مَرْيَمُ أَنَّى﴾ from where ﴿لَكِ هَذَا قَالَتْ﴾ while she was small ﴿هُوَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ﴾ He brings it to me from Paradise ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ﴾ ample provision without consequence.

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿هُنَالِكَ﴾ that is, when Zakariyyā saw that and knew that the One able to bring a thing out of its season is able to bring a child in old age — and the people of his house had died out — ﴿دَعَا زَكَرِيَّاءُ [زَكَرِيَّا] رَبَّهُ﴾ when he entered the prayer chamber (miḥrāb) to pray in the depth of the night ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ هَبْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ﴾ from You ﴿ذُرِّيَّةً طَيِّبَةً﴾ a righteous child ﴿إِنَّكَ سَمِيعُ﴾ the Answerer of ﴿الدُّعَاءِ﴾

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿فَنَادَتْهُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ﴾ that is, Jibrīl ﴿وَهُوَ قَائِمٌ يُصَلِّي فِي الْمِحْرَابِ﴾ that is, the place of worship ﴿أَنَّ﴾ that is, «بِأَنَّ» ("with the news that"); and in one reading with kasra, with "saying" implied ﴿اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكَ﴾ with doubling and without ﴿بِيَحْيَى مُصَدِّقًا بِكَلِمَةٍ﴾ which is ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ that is, in ʿĪsā, that he is the Spirit of Allah; he was called a Word because he was created by the word "Be" ﴿وَسَيِّدًا﴾ followed ﴿وَحَصُورًا﴾ withheld from women ﴿وَنَبِيًّا مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ It is narrated that he never committed a sin nor intended one.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ أَنَّى﴾ how ﴿يَكُونُ لِي غُلَامٌ﴾ a son ﴿وَقَدْ بَلَغَنِيَ الْكِبَرُ﴾ that is, I have reached the end of life, a hundred and twenty years ﴿وَامْرَأَتِي عَاقِرٌ﴾ she had reached ninety-eight years ﴿قَالَ﴾ the matter is ﴿كَذَلِكَ﴾ of Allah creating a son from the two of you ﴿اللَّهُ يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَاءُ﴾ nothing prevents Him from it. To display this great power He inspired him to ask, so that he would be answered with it. And when his soul longed for the swift arrival of what he had been given tidings of,

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ اجْعَلْ لِي آيَةً﴾ that is, a sign of my wife's pregnancy ﴿قَالَ آيَتُكَ﴾ of it ﴿أَنْ لَا تُكَلِّمَ النَّاسَ﴾ that is, you will be withheld from speaking to them, unlike the remembrance of Allah the Exalted ﴿ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ﴾ that is, with their nights ﴿إِلَّا رَمْزًا﴾ by gesture ﴿وَاذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ كَثِيرًا وَسَبِّحْ﴾ pray ﴿بِالْعَشِيِّ وَالْإِبْكَارِ﴾ the ends of the day and its beginnings.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿وَ﴾ mention ﴿إِذْ قَالَتِ الْمَلَائِكَةُ﴾ that is, Jibrīl ﴿يَا مَرْيَمُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفَاكِ﴾ chose you ﴿وَطَهَّرَكِ﴾ from the touch of men ﴿وَاصْطَفَاكِ عَلَى نِسَاءِ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ that is, the people of your time.

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿يَا مَرْيَمُ اقْنُتِي لِرَبِّكِ﴾ obey Him ﴿وَاسْجُدِي وَارْكَعِي مَعَ الرَّاكِعِينَ﴾ that is, pray with those who pray.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ what has been mentioned of the affair of Zakariyyā and Maryam ﴿مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الْغَيْبِ﴾ reports of what was hidden from you ﴿نُوحِيهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾ O Muḥammad ﴿وَمَا كُنْتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ يُلْقُونَ أَقْلَامَهُمْ﴾ into the water, casting lots so that it would become clear to them ﴿أَيُّهُمْ يَكْفُلُ﴾ would raise ﴿مَرْيَمَ وَمَا كُنْتَ لَدَيْهِمْ إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ﴾ over her guardianship, so that you might know it and report it; you have known it only by way of revelation. Mention

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿إِذْ قَالَتِ الْمَلَائِكَةُ﴾ that is, Jibrīl ﴿يَا مَرْيَمُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكِ بِكَلِمَةٍ مِنْهُ﴾ that is, a son ﴿اسْمُهُ الْمَسِيحُ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ﴾ He addressed her by attributing him to her, to point out that she would bear him without a father, since it is the custom for men to be attributed to their fathers ﴿وَجِيهًا﴾ of high standing ﴿فِي الدُّنْيَا﴾ through prophethood ﴿وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ through intercession and the highest ranks ﴿وَمِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ﴾ to Allah.

celaleyn:171-171.t: ﴿يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ بِنِعْمَةٍ﴾ reward ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ وَفَضْلٍ﴾ an increase upon it ﴿وَأَنَّ﴾ with fatḥa, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to نِعْمَةٍ, and with kasra as a new (resumptive) sentence ﴿اللَّهَ لَا يُضِيعُ أَجْرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ rather He rewards them

celaleyn:172-172.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) ﴿اسْتَجَابُوا لِلَّهِ وَالرَّسُولِ﴾ his call to go out to fight, when Abū Sufyān and his companions wanted to return, and they had made an appointment with the Prophet ﷺ and his companions for the market of Badr in the year following the day of Uḥud ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا أَصَابَهُمُ الْقَرْحُ﴾ at Uḥud; and the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ is ﴿لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا مِنْهُمْ﴾ through obedience to Him ﴿وَاتَّقَوْا﴾ disobeying Him ﴿أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ which is the Garden

celaleyn:173-173.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a badal (substitute) for the الَّذِينَ before it, or a naʿt (adjective) ﴿قَالَ لَهُمُ النَّاسُ﴾ i.e. Nuʿaym ibn Masʿūd al-Ashjaʿī ﴿إِنَّ النَّاسَ﴾ Abū Sufyān and his companions ﴿قَدْ جَمَعُوا لَكُمْ﴾ the hosts, to annihilate you ﴿فَاخْشَوْهُمْ﴾ and do not go to them ﴿فَزَادَهُمْ﴾ that saying ﴿إِيمَانًا﴾ assent to Allah and certainty ﴿وَقَالُوا حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ﴾ He suffices us in their matter ﴿وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ﴾ the one to whom the matter is entrusted is He. And they went out with the Prophet ﷺ and arrived at the market of Badr, and Allah cast terror into the heart of Abū Sufyān and his companions, so they did not come. They had merchandise with them, so they sold and made a profit.

celaleyn:174-174.t: He the Exalted said: ﴿فَانْقَلَبُوا﴾ they returned from Badr ﴿بِنِعْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَفَضْلٍ﴾ with safety and profit ﴿لَمْ يَمْسَسْهُمْ سُوءٌ﴾ of killing or wounding ﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا رِضْوَانَ اللَّهِ﴾ by obeying Him and His Messenger in going out ﴿وَاللَّهُ ذُو فَضْلٍ عَظِيمٍ﴾ towards the people of obedience to Him

celaleyn:175-175.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا ذَلِكُمُ﴾ i.e. the one who says to you "إِنَّ النَّاسَ…" etc. ﴿الشَّيْطَانُ يُخَوِّفُ﴾ you ﴿أَوْلِيَاءَهُ﴾ the disbelievers ﴿فَلَا تَخَافُوهُمْ وَخَافُونِ﴾ in abandoning My command ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ truly

celaleyn:176-176.t: ﴿وَلَا يُحْزِنْكَ﴾ with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the zāy, and with fatḥa on it and ḍamma on the zāy [وَلَا يَحْزُنْكَ], from حَزَنَهُ, a dialectal variant of أَحْزَنَهُ ﴿الَّذِينَ يُسَارِعُونَ فِي الْكُفْرِ﴾ falling into it quickly by supporting it; and they are the people of Mecca or the hypocrites, i.e. do not be concerned at their disbelief ﴿إِنَّهُمْ لَنْ يَضُرُّوا اللَّهَ شَيْئًا﴾ by their deeds; rather they harm only themselves ﴿يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَلَّا يَجْعَلَ لَهُمْ حَظًّا﴾ a share ﴿فِي الْآخِرَةِ﴾ i.e. the Garden; that is why He forsook them ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ in the Fire

celaleyn:177-177.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ اشْتَرَوُا الْكُفْرَ بِالْإِيمَانِ﴾ i.e. took it in its place ﴿لَنْ يَضُرُّوا اللَّهَ﴾ by their disbelief ﴿شَيْئًا وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful

celaleyn:178-178.t: ﴿وَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّ﴾ with yāʾ and tāʾ ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّمَا نُمْلِي﴾ i.e. Our granting respite ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ by lengthening their lives and deferring them ﴿خَيْرٌ لِأَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ And أَنَّ with its two governed elements takes the place of the two objects in the reading with the lower-dotted letter [Translator's note: yāʾ], and the place of the second in the other ﴿إِنَّمَا نُمْلِي﴾ We give respite ﴿لَهُمْ لِيَزْدَادُوا إِثْمًا﴾ through many acts of disobedience ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مُهِينٌ﴾ involving humiliation, in the Hereafter

celaleyn:179-179.t: ﴿مَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيَذَرَ﴾ to leave ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَى مَا أَنْتُمْ﴾ O people ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ of the mixing of the sincere with others ﴿حَتَّى يَمِيزَ﴾ with the single (unstressed) and the doubled reading: separate ﴿الْخَبِيثَ﴾ the hypocrite ﴿مِنَ الطَّيِّبِ﴾ the believer, through the arduous obligations that make that clear; and He did that on the day of Uḥud ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُطْلِعَكُمْ عَلَى الْغَيْبِ﴾ so that you would recognise the hypocrite from others before the separation ﴿وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ يَجْتَبِي﴾ chooses ﴿مِنْ رُسُلِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ and acquaints him with His unseen, as He acquainted the Prophet ﷺ with the state of the hypocrites ﴿فَآمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَإِنْ تُؤْمِنُوا وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ hypocrisy ﴿فَلَكُمْ أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:180-180.t: ﴿وَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّ﴾ with yāʾ and tāʾ ﴿الَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ بِمَا آتَاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ i.e. with its zakat ﴿هُوَ﴾ i.e. their miserliness ﴿خَيْرًا لَهُمْ﴾ the second object; the pronoun refers to the bounty, and the first object is "their miserliness" (بُخْلَهُمْ), implied before the relative noun in the reading with the upper-dotted letter [Translator's note: tāʾ] and before the pronoun in the reading with the lower-dotted letter [Translator's note: yāʾ] ﴿بَلْ هُوَ شَرٌّ لَهُمْ سَيُطَوَّقُونَ مَا بَخِلُوا بِهِ﴾ i.e. its zakat, of wealth ﴿يَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ﴾ by its being made into a snake around his neck that bites him, as has come in the hadith ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مِيرَاثُ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ He inherits them after their inhabitants perish ﴿وَاللَّهُ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ with yāʾ and tāʾ [تَعْمَلُونَ] ﴿خَبِيرٌ﴾ so He will recompense you for it

celaleyn:181-181.t: ﴿لَقَدْ سَمِعَ اللَّهُ قَوْلَ الَّذِينَ قَالُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ فَقِيرٌ وَنَحْنُ أَغْنِيَاءُ﴾ and they are the Jews; they said it when {مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًا} ("Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan?") was revealed, and they said: "If He were rich, He would not ask us for a loan." ﴿سَنَكْتُبُ﴾ We will command the writing of ﴿مَا قَالُوا﴾ in the scrolls of their deeds, so that they are recompensed for it; and in one reading it is with yāʾ, passive ﴿وَ﴾ We will write ﴿قَتْلَهُمْ﴾ in the accusative and the nominative ﴿الْأَنْبِيَاءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ وَنَقُولُ﴾ with nūn and yāʾ, i.e. Allah [Translator's note: will say] to them in the Hereafter on the tongues of the angels ﴿ذُوقُوا عَذَابَ الْحَرِيقِ﴾ the Fire. And it will be said to them when they are cast into it:

celaleyn:182-182.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ punishment ﴿بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ﴾ the person is expressed by them because most deeds are performed with them ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلَّامٍ﴾ i.e. one who does wrong ﴿لِلْعَبِيدِ﴾ so as to punish them without sin

celaleyn:183-183.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of the الَّذِينَ before it ﴿قَالُوا﴾ to Muhammad ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ has (qad) ﴿عَهِدَ إِلَيْنَا﴾ in the Torah [Translator's note: the source text opens a ﴿ bracket before عَهِدَ إِلَيْنَا and does not close it before "in the Torah"; the gloss is read here as the commentator's words.] ﴿أَلَّا نُؤْمِنَ لِرَسُولٍ﴾ believe him ﴿حَتَّى يَأْتِيَنَا بِقُرْبَانٍ تَأْكُلُهُ النَّارُ﴾ so we will not believe you until you bring it to us. It is that by which one draws near to Allah, of livestock and other things: if it was accepted, a white fire came from the sky and burned it, otherwise it remained in its place. That was enjoined upon the Children of Israel, except in the case of the Messiah and Muhammad. He the Exalted said: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them in rebuke ﴿قَدْ جَاءَكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِنْ قَبْلِي بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾ with the miracles ﴿وَبِالَّذِي قُلْتُمْ﴾ such as Zakariyyā and Yaḥyā, and you killed them. The address is to those in the time of our Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, even though the deed was their forefathers', because they were pleased with it ﴿فَلِمَ قَتَلْتُمُوهُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ in that you would believe when it is brought

celaleyn:184-184.t: ﴿فَإِنْ كَذَّبُوكَ فَقَدْ كُذِّبَ رُسُلٌ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ جَاءُوا بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾ the miracles ﴿وَالزُّبُرِ﴾ such as the scrolls of Ibrāhīm ﴿وَالْكِتَابِ﴾ and in one reading with the bāʾ retained in both [Translator's note: i.e. وَبِالزُّبُرِ وَبِالْكِتَابِ] ﴿الْمُنِيرِ﴾ the clear, which is the Torah and the Gospel; so be patient as they were patient

celaleyn:185-185.t: ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ وَإِنَّمَا تُوَفَّوْنَ أُجُورَكُمْ﴾ the recompense of your deeds ﴿يَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ فَمَنْ زُحْزِحَ﴾ is removed far ﴿عَنِ النَّارِ وَأُدْخِلَ الْجَنَّةَ فَقَدْ فَازَ﴾ has attained the utmost of what he sought ﴿وَمَا الْحَيَوةُ الدُّنْيَا﴾ i.e. living in it ﴿إِلَّا مَتَاعُ الْغُرُورِ﴾ the vain, enjoyed for a little while and then it perishes

celaleyn:186-186.t: ﴿لَتُبْلَوُنَّ﴾ the nūn of the nominative (nūn al-rafʿ) has been omitted from it because of the succession of nūns, and the wāw that is the plural pronoun [Translator's note: i.e. was omitted as well] because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; i.e. you will surely be tested ﴿فِي أَمْوَالِكُمْ﴾ by the obligations in them and by calamities ﴿وَأَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾ by acts of worship and trial ﴿وَلَتَسْمَعُنَّ مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ﴾ the Jews and the Christians ﴿وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا﴾ among the Arabs ﴿أَذًى كَثِيرًا﴾ of insult, defamation and amorous verses about your women ﴿وَإِنْ تَصْبِرُوا﴾ on that ﴿وَتَتَّقُوا﴾ Allah ﴿فَإِنَّ ذَلِكَ مِنْ عَزْمِ الْأُمُورِ﴾ i.e. among the matters resolved upon, which one resolves upon because they are obligatory

celaleyn:187-187.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ﴾ i.e. the covenant upon them in the Torah ﴿لَيُبَيِّنُنَّهُ﴾ i.e. the Book ﴿لِلنَّاسِ وَلَا يَكْتُمُونَهُ﴾ i.e. the Book; with yāʾ and tāʾ in both verbs [لَتُبَيِّنُنَّهُ لِلنَّاسِ وَلَا تَكْتُمُونَهُ] ﴿فَنَبَذُوهُ﴾ they cast the covenant ﴿وَرَاءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ﴾ and did not act on it ﴿وَاشْتَرَوْا بِهِ﴾ took in its place ﴿ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا﴾ of this world, from their lowly followers, by virtue of their leadership in knowledge; so they concealed it for fear of losing that ﴿فَبِئْسَ مَا يَشْتَرُونَ﴾ this purchase of theirs

celaleyn:188-188.t: ﴿لَا تَحْسَبَنَّ﴾ with tāʾ and yāʾ ﴿الَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِمَا أَتَوْا﴾ did in misleading people ﴿وَيُحِبُّونَ أَنْ يُحْمَدُوا بِمَا لَمْ يَفْعَلُوا﴾ of holding fast to the truth, while they are in misguidance ﴿فَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّهُمْ﴾ in both ways; a tawkīd (emphasis) ﴿بِمَفَازَةٍ﴾ in a place where they will be saved ﴿مِنَ الْعَذَابِ﴾ of the Hereafter; rather they are in a place where they are punished, which is Hell ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful, in it. The two objects of the first يَحْسَبُ are indicated by the two objects of the second in the reading with the lower-dotted letter [Translator's note: yāʾ], and in the reading with the upper-dotted letter [Translator's note: tāʾ] only the second is omitted

celaleyn:189-189.t: ﴿وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ the treasuries of rain, provision, vegetation and other things ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ including punishing the disbelievers and saving the believers

celaleyn:190-190.t: ﴿إِنَّ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ and the wonders in them ﴿وَاخْتِلَافِ الَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ﴾ in coming and going, and increasing and decreasing ﴿لَآيَاتٍ﴾ indications of His power, Exalted is He ﴿لِأُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ﴾ for those possessed of intellect

celaleyn:191-191.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of what precedes it, or a badal (substitute) ﴿يَذْكُرُونَ اللَّهَ قِيَامًا وَقُعُودًا وَعَلَى جُنُوبِهِمْ﴾ lying down, i.e. in every state; and from Ibn ʿAbbās: they pray in these ways according to their ability ﴿وَيَتَفَكَّرُونَ فِي خَلْقِ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ so as to infer from it the power of their Maker, saying: ﴿رَبَّنَا مَا خَلَقْتَ هَذَا﴾ creation which we see ﴿بَاطِلًا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial): in vain, but rather as a proof of the perfection of Your power ﴿سُبْحَانَكَ﴾ declaring You free of acting in vain ﴿فَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ﴾

celaleyn:192-192.t: ﴿رَبَّنَا إِنَّكَ مَنْ تُدْخِلِ النَّارَ﴾ to abide in it forever ﴿فَقَدْ أَخْزَيْتَهُ﴾ You have humiliated him ﴿وَمَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ﴾ the disbelievers; in it the overt noun is put in the place of the pronoun, to indicate that disgrace is specific to them ﴿مِنْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida) ﴿أَنْصَارٍ﴾ who would protect them from the punishment of Allah the Exalted

celaleyn:193-193.t: ﴿رَبَّنَا إِنَّنَا سَمِعْنَا مُنَادِيًا يُنَادِي﴾ calling people ﴿لِلْإِيمَانِ﴾ i.e. to it; and he is Muhammad, or it is the Quran ﴿أَنْ﴾ i.e. "that" (bi-an) ﴿آمِنُوا بِرَبِّكُمْ فَآمَنَّا﴾ in him ﴿رَبَّنَا فَاغْفِرْ لَنَا ذُنُوبَنَا وَكَفِّرْ﴾ cover ﴿عَنَّا سَيِّئَاتِنَا﴾ and do not expose them by punishing for them ﴿وَتَوَفَّنَا﴾ take our souls ﴿مَعَ﴾ among the company of ﴿الْأَبْرَارِ﴾ the prophets and the righteous

celaleyn:194-194.t: ﴿رَبَّنَا وَآتِنَا﴾ give us ﴿مَا وَعَدْتَنَا﴾ thereof ﴿عَلَى﴾ the tongues of ﴿رُسُلِكَ﴾ of mercy and bounty. Their asking for that, even though His promise, Exalted is He, is not broken, is a request that He make them among those deserving it, because they were not certain of their deserving it; and the repetition of رَبَّنَا is for emphasis in supplication ﴿وَلَا تُخْزِنَا يَوْمَ الْقِيَمَةِ إِنَّكَ لَا تُخْلِفُ الْمِيعَادَ﴾ the promise of resurrection and recompense

celaleyn:195-195.t: ﴿فَاسْتَجَابَ لَهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ﴾ their supplication ﴿أَنِّي﴾ i.e. "that I" (bi-annī) ﴿لَا أُضِيعُ عَمَلَ عَامِلٍ مِنْكُمْ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنْثَى بَعْضُكُمْ﴾ being ﴿مِنْ بَعْضٍ﴾ i.e. males from females and vice versa. The sentence confirms what precedes it, i.e. they are equal in being recompensed for deeds and in their not being lost. It was revealed when Umm Salama said: "O Messenger of Allah, I do not hear women mentioned at all in connection with the emigration." ﴿فَالَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا﴾ from Mecca to Medina ﴿وَأُخْرِجُوا مِنْ دِيَارِهِمْ وَأُوذُوا فِي سَبِيلِي﴾ My religion ﴿وَقَاتَلُوا﴾ the disbelievers ﴿وَقُتِلُوا﴾ with the single (unstressed) and the doubled reading, and in one reading with it placed first ﴿لَأُكَفِّرَنَّ عَنْهُمْ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ﴾ I will cover them with forgiveness ﴿وَلَأُدْخِلَنَّهُمْ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ ثَوَابًا﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun) from the meaning of لَأُكَفِّرَنَّ, emphasising it ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ﴾ in it there is a shift (iltifāt) away from the first person ﴿وَاللَّهُ عِنْدَهُ حُسْنُ الثَّوَابِ﴾ recompense. And the following was revealed when the Muslims said: "The enemies of Allah are in the prosperity we see, while we are in hardship":

celaleyn:196-196.t: ﴿لَا يَغُرَّنَّكَ تَقَلُّبُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ their going about ﴿فِي الْبِلَادِ﴾ in trade and earning; it is

celaleyn:197-197.t: ﴿مَتَاعٌ قَلِيلٌ﴾ which they enjoy a little in this world and it perishes ﴿ثُمَّ مَأْوَاهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ﴾ the resting place is it

celaleyn:198-198.t: ﴿لَكِنِ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا رَبَّهُمْ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ خَالِدِينَ﴾ i.e. with abiding decreed for them ﴿فِيهَا نُزُلًا﴾ it is what is prepared for a guest; its accusative is as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from جَنَّاتٌ, and what governs it is the sense of the adverbial phrase (al-ẓarf) ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وَمَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ of reward ﴿خَيْرٌ لِلْأَبْرَارِ﴾ than the enjoyment of this world

celaleyn:199-199.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ لَمَنْ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ﴾ such as ʿAbdullāh ibn Salām and his companions, and the Negus ﴿وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿وَمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ i.e. the Torah and the Gospel ﴿خَاشِعِينَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun of يُؤْمِنُ, with the meaning of مَنْ taken into account [Translator's note: hence the plural], i.e. humble ﴿لِلَّهِ لَا يَشْتَرُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ which they have in the Torah and the Gospel, describing the Prophet ﷺ ﴿ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا﴾ of this world, by concealing them out of fear for their leadership, as others among the Jews do ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ أَجْرُهُمْ﴾ the reward of their deeds ﴿عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ they are given it twice, as in al-Qaṣaṣ

celaleyn:200-200.t: [Translator's note: the opening words below are the end of ayah 199 in the muṣḥaf; the source entry begins with them.] ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ﴾ He brings creation to account in the space of half a day of the days of this world ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اصْبِرُوا﴾ in acts of obedience and in calamities, and [Translator's note: in refraining] from acts of disobedience ﴿وَصَابِرُوا﴾ the disbelievers, so that they are not more patient than you ﴿وَرَابِطُوا﴾ persevere in jihad ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ in all your states ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾ succeed in attaining the Garden and are saved from the Fire

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿وَيُكَلِّمُ النَّاسَ فِي الْمَهْدِ﴾ that is, as an infant, before the age of speech ﴿وَكَهْلًا وَمِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿قَالَتْ رَبِّ أَنَّى﴾ how ﴿يَكُونُ لِي وَلَدٌ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِي بَشَرٌ﴾ through marriage or otherwise ﴿قَالَ﴾ the matter is ﴿كَذَلِكِ﴾ of creating a child from you without a father ﴿اللَّهُ يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَاءُ إِذَا قَضَى أَمْرًا﴾ wills to create it ﴿فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾ that is, and so it is.

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿وَنُعَلِّمُهُ﴾ with nūn and with yāʾ [وَيُعَلِّمُهُ] ﴿الْكِتَابَ﴾ writing ﴿وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَالتَّوْرَاةَ وَالْإِنْجِيلَ﴾

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿وَ﴾ We shall make him ﴿رَسُولًا إِلَى بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾ in childhood or after reaching maturity. Then Jibrīl blew into the opening of her garment and she conceived; and of her story there happened what is mentioned in Sūrat Maryam. When Allah sent him to the Children of Israel, he said to them: "I am the Messenger of Allah to you, ﴿أَنِّي﴾ that is, «بِأَنِّي» ("with the fact that") ﴿قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِآيَةٍ﴾ a sign of my truthfulness ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ it is ﴿أَنِّي﴾ and in one reading with kasra, as resumptive (istiʾnāf) ﴿أَخْلُقُ﴾ I shape ﴿لَكُمْ مِنَ الطِّينِ كَهَيْئَةِ الطَّيْرِ﴾ like its form; so the kāf is a noun, a mafʿūl (object) ﴿فَأَنْفُخُ فِيهِ﴾ the pronoun refers to the kāf ﴿فَيَكُونُ طَيْرًا﴾ and in one reading [طَائِرًا] ﴿بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ by His will." So he created for them the bat, because it is the most perfect of birds in form; it would fly while they watched it, and when it disappeared from their sight it fell dead. ﴿وَأُبْرِئُ﴾ I heal ﴿الْأَكْمَهَ﴾ the one born blind ﴿وَالْأَبْرَصَ﴾ the two are singled out for mention because they are incurable diseases; his mission was in an age of medicine, and he healed fifty thousand in one day by supplication, on condition of faith ﴿وَأُحْيِي الْمَوْتَى بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ He repeated it to dispel any notion of divinity in him. He revived ʿĀzar, a friend of his, the son of the old woman and the daughter of the tithe-collector, and they lived and had children; and Sām son of Nūḥ, who died immediately. ﴿وَأُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا تَأْكُلُونَ وَمَا تَدَّخِرُونَ﴾ hide ﴿فِي بُيُوتِكُمْ﴾ of what I have not seen. He would tell a person what he had eaten and what he would eat later. ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ﴾ what has been mentioned ﴿لَآيَةً لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿وَ﴾ I have come to you ﴿مُصَدِّقًا لِمَا بَيْنَ يَدَيَّ﴾ before me ﴿مِنَ التَّوْرَاةِ وَلِأُحِلَّ لَكُمْ بَعْضَ الَّذِي حُرِّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ in it. So he made lawful for them fish and birds that have no spur. And it is said that he made all of it lawful, so «بَعْض» ("some") is in the sense of «كُلّ» ("all"). ﴿وَجِئْتُكُمْ بِآيَةٍ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ He repeated it for tawkīd (emphasis) and in order to build on it: ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾ in what I command you of the oneness of Allah and obedience to Him.

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ هَذَا﴾ which I command you ﴿صِرَاطٌ﴾ a path ﴿مُسْتَقِيمٌ﴾ But they denied him and did not believe in him.

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا أَحَسَّ﴾ knew ﴿عِيسَى مِنْهُمُ الْكُفْرَ﴾ and they wanted to kill him ﴿قَالَ مَنْ أَنْصَارِي﴾ my helpers, going ﴿إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾ to help His religion ﴿قَالَ الْحَوَارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أَنْصَارُ اللَّهِ﴾ the helpers of His religion. They were the chosen followers of ʿĪsā, the first to believe in him, twelve men; [the name is] from ḥawar, which is pure whiteness; and it is said they were fullers who whitened (yuḥawwirūna) clothes, that is, bleached them. ﴿آمَنَّا﴾ we believe ﴿بِاللَّهِ وَاشْهَدْ﴾ O ʿĪsā ﴿بِأَنَّا مُسْلِمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿رَبَّنَا آمَنَّا بِمَا أَنْزَلْتَ﴾ of the Gospel ﴿وَاتَّبَعْنَا الرَّسُولَ﴾ ʿĪsā ﴿فَاكْتُبْنَا مَعَ الشَّاهِدِينَ﴾ to You with oneness and to Your Messenger with truthfulness. The Exalted said:

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿وَمَكَرُوا﴾ that is, the disbelievers of the Children of Israel against ʿĪsā, when they appointed someone to kill him by stealth ﴿وَمَكَرَ اللَّهُ﴾ against them, by casting ʿĪsā's likeness onto the one who set out to kill him, so they killed him, and ʿĪsā was raised to heaven ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْمَاكِرِينَ﴾ the most knowing of them in it. Mention

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ اللَّهُ يَا عِيسَى إِنِّي مُتَوَفِّيكَ﴾ taking you ﴿وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ﴾ from this world without death ﴿وَمُطَهِّرُكَ﴾ removing you ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَجَاعِلُ الَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوكَ﴾ who affirmed your prophethood, of the Muslims and the Christians ﴿فَوْقَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ in you, and they are the Jews; they will be above them by proof and by the sword ﴿إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَأَحْكُمُ بَيْنَكُمْ فِيمَا كُنْتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ﴾ in the matter of religion.

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَأُعَذِّبُهُمْ عَذَابًا شَدِيدًا فِي الدُّنْيَا﴾ by killing, captivity and the jizya ﴿وَالْآخِرَةِ﴾ by the Fire ﴿وَمَا لَهُمْ مِنْ نَاصِرِينَ﴾ protecting them from it.

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ فَيُوَفِّيهِمْ﴾ with yāʾ and with nūn ﴿أُجُورَهُمْ وَاللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ that is, He will punish them. It is narrated that Allah the Exalted sent him a cloud which raised him up; his mother clung to him and wept, and he said to her: "The Resurrection will bring us together." That was on the Night of Decree (laylat al-qadr) in Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis), when he was thirty-three years old, and his mother lived six years after him. The two Shaykhs [al-Bukhārī and Muslim] narrated the hadith "that he will descend near the Hour, judge by the law of our Prophet, kill the Antichrist (al-Dajjāl) and the swine, break the cross and abolish the jizya." In a hadith of Muslim, he will remain seven years, and in a hadith from Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī, forty years; then he will die and be prayed over. It may be that what is meant [by forty] is the total of his stay on earth before being raised and after.

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ what has been mentioned of the affair of ʿĪsā ﴿نَتْلُوهُ﴾ We relate it ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾ O Muḥammad ﴿مِنَ الْآيَاتِ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in «نَتْلُوهُ», and what governs it (its ʿāmil) is the meaning of pointing contained in «ذَلِكَ» ﴿وَالذِّكْرِ الْحَكِيمِ﴾ the precise one, that is, the Quran.

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿إِنَّ مَثَلَ عِيسَى﴾ his extraordinary case ﴿عِنْدَ اللَّهِ كَمَثَلِ آدَمَ﴾ is like his case, in his creation without mother or father. It is a comparison of the extraordinary with the more extraordinary, so as to be more decisive against the opponent and more effective on the soul. ﴿خَلَقَهُ﴾ that is, Ādam, that is, his frame ﴿مِنْ تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ كُنْ﴾ a human being ﴿فَيَكُونُ﴾ that is, and he was. Likewise ʿĪsā: He said to him "Be," without a father, and he was.

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), that is, "the matter of ʿĪsā [is]" ﴿فَلَا تَكُنْ مِنَ الْمُمْتَرِينَ﴾ those who doubt it.

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿فَمَنْ حَاجَّكَ﴾ disputes with you, of the Christians ﴿فِيهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا جَاءَكَ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ﴾ of his affair ﴿فَقُلْ﴾ to them ﴿تَعَالَوْا نَدْعُ أَبْنَاءَنَا وَأَبْنَاءَكُمْ وَنِسَاءَنَا وَنِسَاءَكُمْ وَأَنْفُسَنَا وَأَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ and gather them ﴿ثُمَّ نَبْتَهِلْ﴾ humbly entreat in supplication ﴿فَنَجْعَلْ لَعْنَتَ اللَّهِ عَلَى الْكَاذِبِينَ﴾ by saying: "O Allah, curse the one who lies concerning ʿĪsā." He ﷺ called the delegation of Najrān to that when they disputed with him about it. They said: "Not until we look into our affair; then we will come to you." Their man of judgement said: "You know that he is a prophet, and that no people ever engaged a prophet in mutual cursing (mubāhala) without perishing; so make a truce with the man and leave." They came to the Messenger ﷺ, who had come out with al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥusayn, Fāṭima and ʿAlī, and he had said to them: "When I supplicate, say Āmīn." But they refused to engage in mutual cursing and made peace with him on the basis of the jizya. Narrated by Abū Nuʿaym. From Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "Had those who were to engage in mubāhala gone out, they would have returned finding neither wealth nor family." And it is narrated: "Had they gone out, they would have been burned."
