celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿إِنَّ هَذَا﴾ which has been mentioned ﴿لَهُوَ الْقَصَصُ﴾ the account ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾ in which there is no doubt ﴿وَمَا مِنْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida) ﴿إِلَهٍ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ﴾ in His dominion ﴿الْحَكِيمُ﴾ in His making.

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا﴾ turned away from faith ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ بِالْمُفْسِدِينَ﴾ and will recompense them. In it the overt noun is put in the place of the pronoun.

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿قُلْ يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Jews and Christians ﴿تَعَالَوْا إِلَى كَلِمَةٍ سَوَاءٍ﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of "whose matter is equal" ﴿بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَكُمْ﴾ it is ﴿أَنْ لَا نَعْبُدَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ وَلَا نُشْرِكَ بِهِ شَيْئًا وَلَا يَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُنَا بَعْضًا أَرْبَابًا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ as you have taken the rabbis and monks ﴿فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا﴾ turned away from tawḥīd ﴿فَقُولُوا﴾ you, to them ﴿اشْهَدُوا بِأَنَّا مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ affirmers of Allah's oneness. And when the Jews said, "Ibrāhīm was a Jew and we follow his religion," and the Christians said likewise, there was revealed:

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ لِمَ تُحَاجُّونَ﴾ dispute ﴿فِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ by your claim that he followed your religion ﴿وَمَا أُنْزِلَتِ التَّوْرَاةُ وَالْإِنْجِيلُ إِلَّا مِنْ بَعْدِهِ﴾ by a long time, and Judaism and Christianity arose after they were revealed ﴿أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ the falsity of your claim?

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿هَا﴾ for drawing attention (tanbīh) ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject); O ﴿هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ and the khabar (predicate) is ﴿حَاجَجْتُمْ فِيمَا لَكُمْ بِهِ عِلْمٌ﴾ of the affair of Mūsā and ʿĪsā, and your claim to be of their religion ﴿فَلِمَ تُحَاجُّونَ فِيمَا لَيْسَ لَكُمْ بِهِ عِلْمٌ﴾ of the case of Ibrāhīm ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ﴾ his case ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ The Exalted said, clearing Ibrāhīm:

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿مَا كَانَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ يَهُودِيًّا وَلَا نَصْرَانِيًّا وَلَكِنْ كَانَ حَنِيفًا﴾ inclining away from all religions to the upright religion ﴿مُسْلِمًا﴾ an affirmer of Allah's oneness

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ ﴿إِنَّ أَوْلَى النَّاسِ﴾ the most entitled of them ﴿بِإِبْرَاهِيمَ لَلَّذِينَ اتَّبَعُوهُ﴾ in his time ﴿وَهَذَا النَّبِيُّ﴾ Muḥammad, because he agrees with him in most of his law ﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ of his community; it is they who should say "We follow his religion," not you ﴿وَاللَّهُ وَلِيُّ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ their helper and protector. And when the Jews called Muʿādh, Ḥudhayfa and ʿAmmār to their religion, there was revealed:

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿وَدَّتْ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ لَوْ يُضِلُّونَكُمْ وَمَا يُضِلُّونَ إِلَّا أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ because the sin of their misleading is upon them, and the believers do not obey them in it ﴿وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾ that.

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ لِمَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ the Quran, which contains the description of Muḥammad ﷺ ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ تَشْهَدُونَ﴾ you know that it is true.

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ لِمَ تَلْبِسُونَ﴾ mix ﴿الْحَقَّ بِالْبَاطِلِ﴾ through distortion and falsification ﴿وَتَكْتُمُونَ الْحَقَّ﴾ that is, the description of the Prophet ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that it is true.

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿وَقَالَتْ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ﴾ the Jews, to one another ﴿آمِنُوا بِالَّذِي أُنْزِلَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ that is, the Quran ﴿وَجْهَ النَّهَارِ﴾ its beginning ﴿وَاكْفُرُوا﴾ in it ﴿آخِرَهُ لَعَلَّهُمْ﴾ that is, the believers ﴿يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ from their religion, since they will say: "These people, who are people of knowledge, did not turn back from it after entering it except because they knew it to be false." And they also said:

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿وَلَا تُؤْمِنُوا﴾ do not believe ﴿إِلَّا لِمَنْ﴾ the lām is redundant (zāʾida) ﴿تَبِعَ﴾ conforms to ﴿دِينَكُمْ﴾ The Exalted said: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them, O Muḥammad ﴿إِنَّ الْهُدَى هُدَى اللَّهِ﴾ which is Islam, and everything besides it is error; and the clause is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ) ﴿أَنْ﴾ that is, «بِأَنْ» ("that") ﴿يُؤْتَى أَحَدٌ مِثْلَ مَا أُوتِيتُمْ﴾ of scripture, wisdom and excellences. «أَنْ» is the mafʿūl (object) of «تُؤْمِنُوا», and the one from which exception is made (al-mustathnā minhu) is «أَحَدٌ», with the excepted placed before it. The meaning: do not acknowledge that anyone is given that, except to one who follows your religion ﴿أَوْ﴾ that ﴿يُحَاجُّوكُمْ﴾ that is, the believers will overcome you ﴿عِنْدَ رَبِّكُمْ﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, because you are sounder in religion. In one reading: «أَأَنْ», with the hamza of rebuke; that is, "would you acknowledge that anyone is given the like of it?" The Exalted said: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ الْفَضْلَ بِيَدِ اللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾ so from where do you have it that no one is given the like of what you were given? ﴿وَاللَّهُ وَاسِعٌ﴾ abundant in bounty ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of who deserves it.

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿يَخْتَصُّ بِرَحْمَتِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿وَمِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِقِنْطَارٍ﴾ that is, with much wealth ﴿يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾ because of his trustworthiness, like ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām: a man deposited with him one thousand two hundred ounces of gold and he returned them to him ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ إِنْ تَأْمَنْهُ بِدِينَارٍ لَا يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾ because of his treachery ﴿إِلَّا مَا دُمْتَ عَلَيْهِ قَائِمًا﴾ not leaving him; whenever you leave him he denies it, like Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf: a man of Quraysh deposited a dinar with him and he denied it ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ that is, the failure to return ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ قَالُوا﴾ because of their saying ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْنَا فِي الْأُمِّيِّينَ﴾ that is, the Arabs ﴿سَبِيلٌ﴾ that is, any sin — because they held it lawful to wrong whoever differed from their religion, and they attributed that to Him, Exalted is He. The Exalted said: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ﴾ in attributing that to Him ﴿وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that they are liars.

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿بَلَى﴾ there is against them a way [of blame] concerning them ﴿مَنْ أَوْفَى بِعَهْدِهِ﴾ which he has pledged, or the covenant Allah made with him, of returning trusts and other things ﴿وَاتَّقَى﴾ Allah, by abandoning acts of disobedience and doing acts of obedience ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ In it the overt noun is put in the place of the pronoun; that is, He loves them, in the sense that He rewards them. And it was revealed about the Jews, when they altered the description of the Prophet ﷺ and the covenant Allah made with them in the Torah, and about those who swear falsely in a claim or in selling goods:

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَشْتَرُونَ﴾ exchange ﴿بِعَهْدِ اللَّهِ﴾ with them, regarding faith in the Prophet and the returning of trusts ﴿وَأَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾ their swearing by Him, Exalted is He, falsely ﴿ثَمَنًا قَلِيلًا﴾ of this world ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَا خَلَاقَ﴾ share ﴿لَهُمْ فِي الْآخِرَةِ وَلَا يُكَلِّمُهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ out of anger at them ﴿وَلَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ have mercy on them ﴿يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَلَا يُزَكِّيهِمْ﴾ purify them ﴿وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful.

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ مِنْهُمْ﴾ that is, the People of the Book ﴿لَفَرِيقًا﴾ a group, such as Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf ﴿يَلْوُونَ أَلْسِنَتَهُمْ بِالْكِتَابِ﴾ that is, in reciting it they bend them away from what was revealed to what they have distorted of the description of the Prophet and the like ﴿لِتَحْسَبُوهُ﴾ that is, the distorted ﴿مِنَ الْكِتَابِ﴾ which Allah revealed ﴿وَمَا هُوَ مِنَ الْكِتَابِ وَيَقُولُونَ هُوَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وَمَا هُوَ مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ وَيَقُولُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ وَهُمْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that they are liars. And it was revealed when the Christians of Najrān said that ʿĪsā had commanded them to take him as a lord, and when some Muslims asked to prostrate to him ﷺ:

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿مَا كَانَ﴾ it is fitting ﴿لِبَشَرٍ أَنْ يُؤْتِيَهُ اللَّهُ الْكِتَابَ وَالْحُكْمَ﴾ that is, understanding of the law ﴿وَالنُّبُوَّةَ ثُمَّ يَقُولَ لِلنَّاسِ كُونُوا عِبَادًا لِي مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَلَكِنْ﴾ he says ﴿كُونُوا رَبَّانِيِّينَ﴾ scholars who act [on their knowledge], attributed to the Lord (al-rabb), with the addition of alif and nūn for magnification ﴿بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ with the light form and with doubling [تُعَلِّمُونَ] ﴿الْكِتَابَ وَبِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَدْرُسُونَ﴾ that is, because of that, for its benefit is that you act. [Translator's note: «مَا كَانَ» is glossed with «يَنْبَغِي» ("it is fitting"), the negation carrying over: "it is not fitting".]

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿وَلَا يَأْمُرَكُمْ﴾ in the nominative (rafʿ) as resumptive (istiʾnāf), that is, Allah; and in the accusative (naṣb) [وَلَا يَأْمُرَكُمْ], conjoined to «يَقُولَ», that is, the human being [Translator's note: the Quranic text and the bracketed variant are both printed in the accusative; the nominative reading is وَلَا يَأْمُرُكُمْ.] ﴿أَنْ تَتَّخِذُوا الْمَلَائِكَةَ وَالنَّبِيِّينَ أَرْبَابًا﴾ as the Sabians took the angels, the Jews ʿUzayr and the Christians ʿĪsā ﴿أَيَأْمُرُكُمْ بِالْكُفْرِ بَعْدَ إِذْ أَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ This does not befit him.

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿وَ﴾ mention ﴿إِذْ﴾ when ﴿أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ النَّبِيِّينَ﴾ their covenant ﴿لَمَا﴾ with fatḥa on the lām, as the lām of commencement (lām al-ibtidāʾ) and to emphasise the meaning of the oath contained in the taking of the covenant; and with kasra, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أَخَذَ». «مَا» is a relative noun on both readings, that is, "that which" ﴿آتَيْتُكُمْ﴾ it; and in one reading [آتَيْنَاكُمْ] ﴿مِنْ كِتَابٍ وَحِكْمَةٍ ثُمَّ جَاءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ مُصَدِّقٌ لِمَا مَعَكُمْ﴾ of scripture and wisdom, and he is Muḥammad ﷺ ﴿لَتُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهِ وَلَتَنْصُرُنَّهُ﴾ the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), if you live to see him; and their communities follow them in that ﴿قَالَ﴾ the Exalted to them ﴿أَأَقْرَرْتُمْ﴾ that ﴿وَأَخَذْتُمْ﴾ accepted ﴿عَلَى ذَلِكُمْ إِصْرِي﴾ My covenant ﴿قَالُوا أَقْرَرْنَا قَالَ فَاشْهَدُوا﴾ to that, against yourselves and your followers ﴿وَأَنَا مَعَكُمْ مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ﴾ against you and against them.

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿فَمَنْ تَوَلَّى﴾ turns away ﴿بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ﴾ covenant ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْفَاسِقُونَ﴾

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿أَفَغَيْرَ دِينِ اللَّهِ يَبْغُونَ﴾ with yāʾ, that is, those who turn away; and with tāʾ ﴿وَلَهُ أَسْلَمَ﴾ submitted ﴿مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ طَوْعًا﴾ without refusal ﴿وَكَرْهًا﴾ by the sword and by seeing what compels them to it ﴿وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ with tāʾ and with yāʾ [يُرْجَعُونَ]. And the hamza is for disapproval (inkār).

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them, O Muḥammad ﴿آمَنَّا بِاللَّهِ وَمَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَيْنَا وَمَا أُنْزِلَ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَالْأَسْبَاطِ﴾ his descendants ﴿وَمَا أُوتِيَ مُوسَى وَعِيسَى وَالنَّبِيُّونَ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْهُمْ﴾ by affirming and denying ﴿وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ sincere in worship. And it was revealed about those who apostatised and joined the disbelievers:

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَبْتَغِ غَيْرَ الْإِسْلَامِ دِينًا فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنْهُ وَهُوَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ مِنَ الْخَاسِرِينَ﴾ because he is bound for the Fire, made everlasting for him.

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿كَيْفَ﴾ that is, [Allah does] not ﴿يَهْدِي اللَّهُ قَوْمًا كَفَرُوا بَعْدَ إِيمَانِهِمْ وَشَهِدُوا﴾ that is, and [after] their testifying ﴿أَنَّ الرَّسُولَ حَقٌّ وَ﴾ already ﴿جَاءَهُمُ الْبَيِّنَاتُ﴾ the manifest proofs of the Prophet's truthfulness ﴿وَاللَّهُ لَا يَهْدِي الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ that is, the disbelievers.

celaleyn:87-87.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ جَزَاؤُهُمْ أَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةَ اللَّهِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا﴾ that is, the curse, or the Fire, which it indicates ﴿لَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمُ الْعَذَابُ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ﴾ given respite.

celaleyn:89-89.t: ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ وَأَصْلَحُوا﴾ their deeds ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ﴾ to them ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ towards them. And there was revealed about the Jews:

celaleyn:90-90.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ in ʿĪsā ﴿بَعْدَ إِيمَانِهِمْ﴾ in Mūsā ﴿ثُمَّ ازْدَادُوا كُفْرًا﴾ in Muḥammad ﴿لَنْ تُقْبَلَ تَوْبَتُهُمْ﴾ when they are at the death-rattle or die as disbelievers ﴿وَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الضَّالُّونَ﴾

celaleyn:91-91.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَمَاتُوا وَهُمْ كُفَّارٌ فَلَنْ يُقْبَلَ مِنْ أَحَدِهِمْ مِلْءُ الْأَرْضِ﴾ the amount that would fill it ﴿ذَهَبًا وَلَوِ افْتَدَى بِهِ﴾ The fāʾ is put into the khabar (predicate) of «إِنَّ» because «الَّذِينَ» resembles a condition, and to signal that the non-acceptance is caused by dying in disbelief. ﴿أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful ﴿وَمَا لَهُمْ مِنْ نَاصِرِينَ﴾ protecting them from it.

celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿لَنْ تَنَالُوا الْبِرَّ﴾ that is, its reward, which is Paradise ﴿حَتَّى تُنْفِقُوا﴾ give in charity ﴿مِمَّا تُحِبُّونَ﴾ of your wealth ﴿وَمَا تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِهِ عَلِيمٌ﴾ and will recompense it. And when the Jews said, "You claim to follow the religion of Ibrāhīm, yet he did not eat the meat of camels or drink their milk," there was revealed:

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿كُلُّ الطَّعَامِ كَانَ حِلًّا﴾ lawful ﴿لِبَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ إِلَّا مَا حَرَّمَ إِسْرَائِيلُ﴾ Yaʿqūb ﴿عَلَى نَفْسِهِ﴾ and that was camels, when he was afflicted with sciatica (ʿirq al-nasā, with fatḥa and the short final alif); he vowed that if he were cured he would not eat them, and so they were forbidden to them ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تُنَزَّلَ التَّوْرَاةُ﴾ and that was after Ibrāhīm; they were not forbidden in his time, as they claimed ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿فَأْتُوا بِالتَّوْرَاةِ فَاتْلُوهَا﴾ so that the truth of your claim may become clear ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ in it. They were dumbfounded and did not bring it. The Exalted said:

celaleyn:94-94.t: ﴿فَمَنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ الْكَذِبَ مِنْ بَعْدِ ذَلِكَ﴾ that is, after the proof has become manifest that the prohibition came only from Yaʿqūb and not in the time of Ibrāhīm ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾ those who overstep the truth to falsehood.

celaleyn:95-95.t: ﴿قُلْ صَدَقَ اللَّهُ﴾ in this, as in everything He has reported ﴿فَاتَّبِعُوا مِلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ which I follow ﴿حَنِيفًا﴾ inclining away from every religion to Islam ﴿وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ الْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ And when they said, "Our qibla came before your qibla," there was revealed:

celaleyn:96-96.t: ﴿إِنَّ أَوَّلَ بَيْتٍ وُضِعَ﴾ as a place of worship ﴿لِلنَّاسِ﴾ on earth ﴿لَلَّذِي بِبَكَّةَ﴾ with bāʾ, a dialectal form of Makka; it is so called because it crushes (tabukku) the necks of tyrants, that is, breaks them. The angels built it before the creation of Ādam, and al-Aqṣā was set up after it, with forty years between them, as in the hadith of the two Ṣaḥīḥs. And in a hadith: "It was the first thing to appear on the face of the water when the heavens and the earth were created, as a white foam, and the earth was spread out from beneath it." ﴿مُبَارَكًا﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الَّذِي», that is, possessing blessing ﴿وَهُدًى لِلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ because it is their qibla.

celaleyn:97-97.t: ﴿فِيهِ آيَاتٌ بَيِّنَاتٌ﴾ among them ﴿مَقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ that is, the stone on which he stood when building the House; his feet left their mark in it, and it has remained to this day despite the passage of time and the many hands that have touched it. Among them also are the multiplication of good deeds in it, and that birds do not fly over it. ﴿وَمَنْ دَخَلَهُ كَانَ آمِنًا﴾ he is not to be molested by killing, wrongdoing or anything else ﴿وَلِلَّهِ عَلَى النَّاسِ حِجُّ الْبَيْتِ﴾ is obligatory — with kasra and fatḥa on the ḥāʾ, two dialectal forms of the maṣdar (verbal noun) of حَجَّ in the sense of "to set out for" — and there is substituted (yubdal) from «النَّاسِ» ﴿مَنِ اسْتَطَاعَ إِلَيْهِ سَبِيلًا﴾ a way; he ﷺ explained it as provisions and a mount, narrated by al-Ḥākim and others ﴿وَمَنْ كَفَرَ﴾ in Allah, or in the Hajj which He made obligatory ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ عَنِ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ mankind, jinn and angels, and their worship.

celaleyn:98-98.t: ﴿قُلْ يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ لِمَ تَكْفُرُونَ بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ﴾ the Quran ﴿وَاللَّهُ شَهِيدٌ عَلَى مَا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ and will recompense you for it.

celaleyn:99-99.t: ﴿قُلْ يَا أَهْلَ الْكِتَابِ لِمَ تَصُدُّونَ﴾ turn away ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ that is, His religion ﴿مَنْ آمَنَ﴾ by your denying the Prophet and concealing his description ﴿تَبْغُونَهَا﴾ that is, seeking the way ﴿عِوَجًا﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of "crooked", that is, deviating from the truth ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ شُهَدَاءُ﴾ knowing that the pleasing, upright religion is the religion of Islam, as is in your scripture ﴿وَمَا اللَّهُ بِغَافِلٍ عَمَّا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ of disbelief and denial; He only defers you until your appointed time in order to recompense you. And when one of the Jews passed by the Aws and Khazraj and was enraged by their harmony, he reminded them of the strife there had been between them in the Jāhiliyya, so they quarrelled and nearly fought one another; there was revealed:
